Furuichi In'ei () was a Japanese Buddhist monk and warrior active from the middle of the Muromachi period into the Sengoku period. He was a (armed monk-retainer) of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province. His father was, and his younger brother was Chōin.

== Life ==
=== Meeting with Kyōkaku and the deaths of his parents ===
He was born the son of, head (tōryō) of the kanpu shuto of the of Kōfuku-ji in Yamato Province.

On 3 March 1447 (Bun'an 4, 2nd month, 17th day), he met for the first time, the abbot (monzeki) of Daijō-in, who had moved into the at Furuichi through his father Insen's arrangements.

On 14 August 1448 (Bun'an 5, 7th month, 15th day), his mother died. The hundredth-day memorial was held on the 26th day of the 10th month.

From 22 June to 7 July 1449 (Hōtoku 1, 6th month, 2nd–17th day), he suffered from a disorder of the stomach and became gravely ill. Kyōkaku wrote: " has a calm disposition, and when he grows up he will surely become a person above the ordinary. Lately he has become all the more attached to me, which makes this all the more pitiful. There is nothing to be done, and I am simply at a loss", and prayed for him again and again. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁] Perhaps because the prayers were answered, showed signs of recovery that dawn, and by the 17th he had fully recovered.

From 25 to 31 May 1450 (Hōtoku 2, 4th month, 14th–20th day), he made a pilgrimage to Ise Grand Shrine together with his grandmother, the nun, and his younger sister. Before departing he received a woven-colour katabira (unlined robe) from Kyōkaku. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、135頁]

On 30 July 1453 (Kyōtoku 2, 6th month, 24th day), his father Insen died, and he became the head (sōryō) of the Furuichi house.

=== Appointment as head of the kanpu shuto ===

On 26 October 1455 (Kōshō 1, 9th month, 16th day), following the downfall of the Tsutsui clan, he was appointed head of the, and, a member of the Furuichi family, became his deputy (daikan). [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、355頁] Until his coming of age (genpuku), devoted himself to temple administration, and other matters were handled by the Furuichi deputies (Yamamura Inkei and ).,, and were also appointed heads of the kanpu shuto. [ref: ] [ref: 興福院所蔵 鷹山家文書調査報告書, 生駒市教育委員会]

On 27 June 1456 (Kōshō 2, 5th month, 25th day), the temple administration notified him that he would receive, as his first stipend, 13 koku of polished rice and 5 kanmon of gratuity money from the Furuichi and estates, shōen belonging to the Furuichi domain. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、44頁] By this time appears already to have been taking part in practical work as a shuto. The following month, on 14 July (6th month, 12th day), an order was issued to Furuichi, Ochi and Koizumi to collect the contributions levied on the temples and shrines of Yamato for the repair of Daijō-in's buildings. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第12巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、207頁] These included Shōryaku-ji,, Hase-dera, Chōgaku-ji, Shigisan-ji, and Tachibana-dera.

On 14 February 1457 (Kōshō 3, 1st month, 20th day), Toyoda Raiei entrusted him with supervising the work on the of the Zenjō-in. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第1巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、75-79頁] To prepare the groundwork, about thirty labourers a day were called up from the seven gō (villages) of the temple's domain, joined by two. On the 19th he went to Hannya-ji with Kyōkaku and.

On the 20th day of the 7th month of the same year, he married a daughter of the Kubojō clan.

In the 3rd month of 1459 (Chōroku 3), his grandmother the nun died, and in the 8th month of the following year his grandfather died.

On 16 March 1460 (Chōroku 4, 2nd month, 23rd day), he met with and other members of the opposing Tsutsui faction. On 22 November (Chōroku 4, 10th month, 10th day), in a battle at Tatsuta in Yamato,, a member of the Furuichi family, and his sons the brothers were killed. [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第2巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、357頁] [ref: 『奈良県史第11巻 大和武士』、奈良県 編者／朝倉弘 著者、1993年、116頁] Yamato was divided by the succession dispute (o-ie sōdō) in the Hatakeyama clan, and the (local landholders) were fighting in support of either Hatakeyama Yoshinari or Hatakeyama Masanaga; In'ei supported Yoshinari together with. and his sons, on Yoshinari's side, attacked Masanaga's camp at Tatsuta (present-day Ikaruga, Ikoma District) but were defeated. Kyōkaku was told that this was because Tsutsui Jun'ei, in the rear of Masanaga's army, had attacked with about 500 men. [ref: 『経覚』、酒井紀美著、2019年、194頁]

=== The dharma name "In'ei"; meeting the Shiba and Asakura ===
On 18 September 1465 (Kanshō 6, 8th month, 28th day), he took the tonsure and adopted the dharma name "In'ei". [ref: 『大乗院寺社雑事記 第3巻』、辻善之助 編・校訂、1964年、518頁] The ordination followed due form: his two preceptors, and, supplied the robes and a full set of garments, and an offering of 300 hiki was made. Before the tonsure he offered a cup of sake in the room of, and afterwards he was granted a bundle of sugihara paper and a roll of white cloth.

Site: Electronics Stack Exchange
Title: If two PCB traces have equal propagation delay, can we say they are phase matched?
Tags: signal-integrity, high-speed

Question:
I am learning length and phase matching from Microchip's High-Speed PCB course.

The slide gives "Typical Microstrip Matching Requirements" with Length Match in mm and Phase Match in mm, with tighter values at higher frequencies, e.g. 1 GHz: 1 mm / 0.25 mm, 10 GHz: 0.1 mm / 0.025 mm.

From discussions I understood:

Length mismatch:

$$\Delta L = |L_B - L_A|$$

Propagation delay:

$$t_d = \frac{L}{v_p}$$
$$v_p = \frac{c}{\sqrt{\varepsilon_{eff}}}$$
$$c = 300 \text{ mm/ns}$$

So skew:

$$\Delta t = \frac{\Delta L}{v_p}$$

Phase difference:

$$\Delta \phi = 360 f \Delta t = 360 f \frac{\Delta L}{v_p}$$

And that equal physical length does NOT guarantee equal delay, because Ereff can differ. For equal delay we need:

$$L_1 \sqrt{\varepsilon_{eff1}} = L_2 \sqrt{\varepsilon_{eff2}}$$

Example: microstrip 100 mm with Ereff=3 needs stripline 86.6 mm with Ereff=4 for same delay, since:

$$100\sqrt{3} = L_B\sqrt{4}$$

What I still don't get:

If I make propagation delays equal (td1 = td2), can I say the two traces are phase matched? Or is phase matching something different that only applies at a specific frequency? For non-dispersive FR4 up to about 10 GHz, is delay matching equivalent to phase matching?

Why does Microchip express phase matching in mm? Phase should be in degrees. I calculated:

$$\Delta L = 0.25 \text{ mm},\quad v_p = 150 \text{ mm/ns}$$
$$\Delta t = \frac{0.25}{150} = 1.67 \text{ ps}$$
$$\Delta \phi = 360 \times 1\text{ GHz} \times 1.67\text{ ps} \approx 0.6^{\circ}$$

Is the mm value just a routing tolerance to limit phase error?

For a differential pair vs a DDR DQ/DQS group, is "phase matching" used to mean intra-pair P/N matching, while "length matching" means matching different pairs/groups?
[truncated]

Answer A:
You have a lot of questions here, so I'll try to answer them individually.

If I make propagation delays equal (td1 = td2), can I say the two traces are phase matched?

Phase and length are related for electromagnetic waves using the equation

$$ \Delta \phi = \frac{2\pi\sqrt{\epsilon _r}}{\lambda _0} \Delta x $$

so if \$\Delta x\$ is 0 (trace lengths are matched in a uniform material), then \$\Delta \phi\$ is also 0 (the phases are matched).

Or is phase matching something different that only applies at a specific frequency? For non-dispersive FR4 up to about 10 GHz, is delay matching equivalent to phase matching?

Note that in the equation above, the wavelength (and therefore frequency) and material need to be constant. However, the equation applies to all frequencies and all materials as long as they are constant.

Why does Microchip express phase matching in mm?

The equation I shared shows a direct relationship between phase and length, so using either one gives you the other. You have to make the assumption that your material is uniform, which isn't the case in FR4, but it's a good approximation for a lot of cases.

Is the mm value just a routing tolerance to limit phase error?

Yes, it's easier as a board designer to check that lengths are matched than to try and calculate the phase difference.

For a differential pair vs a DDR DQ/DQS group, is "phase matching" used to mean intra-pair P/N matching, while "length matching" means matching different pairs/groups?
[truncated]

Answer B:
Delay

It's delay that's the important one, but length matching is easy - the problem is that delay is very hard to accurately calculate (especially up in the GHz).

The primary determiner of delay is the effective dielectric constant and the total length. You have reasonable control over the track length, but total delay changes with:

Binder choice (FR4, Teflon, Alumina etc.)

Filler choice (e-glass fiber, ceramic powder, etc.)

Fiber weave/filler density variation (glass != epoxy)

Fiber weave pattern (dense, loose, dobby, etc.)

Trace thickness (more surface for e-fields to bleed out from)

Trace material (Copper != Gold)

Intra-package skew (if you're lucky, you'll get a table of pin/ps delay pairs)

Discontinuities (AC-coupling caps, vias, connectors, BGA balls etc.)

Surrounding atmosphere (i.e. air, vacuum, re-enterable gell etc.)

Trace geometry (e.g. microstrip vs stripline vs CPWG etc.)

Surface roughness (think "path length")

Surface plating material (ENIG involves Nickle, and being ferrous, has some weird effects)

Temperature (why would Er be the same at +100 as -100? Also, things expand...)

Track vs weave angle (good paper by... Intel? on this somewhere, apparently 15° is good)

Ambient humidity (Did you know water has an Er of around 80?)

Etch effects (wider, thinner, underhang, overhang, etc.)

Proximity of PCB to other conductive objects (enclosures, heatsinks, hands, etc.)

Frequency (for the same reasons prisms make rainbows)

Single-ended vs differential pair (slower leg in the pair drags on faster leg and vice-versa)

You get the idea... So, rather than subject themselves to this infinite rabbit hole, many people instead say "F*** it, keep them on one layer, keep them length-matched, avoid vias, good enough"
[truncated]

Title: Morpheus.AI: agents autonomously generate, execute and refine virtual tissue models

Abstract:
Virtual tissue models link observations to mechanistic hypotheses, but building them demands expertise in biology, mathematics and programming. Here, large language model (LLM) agents paired with the simulator Morpheus (Morpheus.AI) autonomously built such models from fifteen benchmark studies, five without a published model. With a frontier LLM, agents that ran their simulations met 83-86% of study-specific criteria in under two hours and for under US\$4 per model. Such agents could make in silico modeling routine.

Site: Electronics Stack Exchange
Title: what is the purpose of the capacitors in this VFO?
Tags: rf, oscillator, feedback

Question:
I am just stepping into RF electronics, and I was wondering what the purpose of C3 and C4 is in the circuit below.  I know that this type of configuration is supposed to provide feedback into the circuit, but I don't understand why there are two capacitors connected the way that they are.

source:
https://www.qsl.net/va3iul/High_Frequency_VCO_Design_and_Schematics/High_Frequency_VCO_Design_and_Schematics.htm

I also have a similar configuration in other circuits such as crystal oscillators, and I am curious if they serve the same purpose.  See C1 and C2 in the parallel resonance circuit below:

Source: https://savantgarde.org/the-piezoelectric-crystal-oscillator/

Answer A:
Resonant current flows around the loop shown below:

 All the capacitors in that loop (C1, C2+D1, C3, C4) are in series: their equivalent capacitance (slightly less the 1 pf) resonate with L1 near 1.1 GHz.

Neglecting Q1's effect, C3 & C4 would form a capacitive voltage divider, since their resonant currents are equal, and in-phase.

C3 would have 8/(6+8) = 57.1% of Q1's base voltage

C4 would have 6/(6+8) = 42.9% of Q1's base voltage

However, Q1 is an emitter follower, whose ideal voltage gain is +1. Can you see that the voltage ratio described above will be disturbed? C4 gets a boost of current from Q1's emitter, in-phase with Q1's base voltage. This is positive feedback that maintains oscillation.

The calculations above are crude: Q1 adds some of its own capacitance, C5 also affects frequency. L2 and R2 have fairly high impedance that doesn't carry much resonant current, so I've neglected their contribution.

C1, C2 along with L1 dominate as far as resonance is concerned. Sometimes, you'll see C3 missing entirely, depending on the transistor's base-to-emitter capacitance instead.

As for the other oscillator, the transistor is operated as a common-base, where the base is grounded via the unlabeled capacitor with a large value. The relationship between emitter and collector is in-phase again, since common-base transistors have a positive voltage gain that is usually greater than one.

The left-most circuit usually resonates L1 with the series-combination of C1, C2. Transistor collector is at a high impedance and quite large voltage at the resonating frequency. C2>C1 so that the emitter sees a low impedance. If the crystal is replaced with its series-equivalent resistance at its SERIES-resonant frequency, the circuit should still oscillate.

I've not seen the right-most circuit in the wild. Over a small frequency span, the crystal is inductive, causing a parallel-resonance with the two capacitors C1, C2. Again C2>C1.

You might want the series-equivalent capacitance of C1, C2 to equal the crystal-manufacturer's loading capacitance if you want oscillations to be at the manufacturer's target frequency.
[truncated]

Answer B:
The tutorial clearly states the VFO uses a Colpitts oscillator configuration. A Colpitts oscillator obtains correctly-phased feedback through a tuned tank circuit with a coil (or crystal) and two capacitors.

"The... transistor amplifier... output signal [is] 180° out of phase with regards to the input signal. The additional 180° phase shift require[d] for oscillation is achieved by the fact that the two capacitors are connected together in series but in parallel with the inductive coil resulting in overall phase shift of the circuit being zero or 360°," as explained at ElectronicsTuitorials.

Note that C1, C2, C3 and C4 are all in series with L1, and therefore affect tuning and are part of the tank circuit. That said, C1 and C2 are smaller, so primarily determine frequency, while C3 are C4 are used primarily to determine feedback phasing... but they do affect tuning, with roughly 1/3 the effect of the other two capacitors and the varactor diode.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Closed form for the probability of exactly $k$ loops when randomly tying $n$ shoelaces
Tags: probability, probability-theory, probability-distributions, random-variables

Question:
A box contains $n$ shoelaces. At each step, two free ends are chosen uniformly at random and tied together. This continues until there are no free ends  (A completed loop may contain one or several original shoelaces). Let $L_n$ denote the final number of loops. I would like to find the probability distribution $p_n(k)=\mathbb{P}(L_n=k)$, $1\le k\le n$.

The expected number of loops is discussed in these questions [1,2,3]. These give $\mathbb E[L_n]=\sum_{m=1}^n\frac1{2m-1}$. My question concerns the individual probabilities $p_n(k)$. I have obtained the following recurrence: Initially, there are $2n$ free ends, and the probability that the first tie closes a loop is $n/\binom{2n}{2}=\frac1{2n-1}$. If the first tie closes a loop, there are $n-1$ open shoelaces left, together with one completed loop. Otherwise, it joins two shoelaces into one longer open chain, again leaving $n-1$ open shoelaces. Therefore,
$$p_n(k)=\frac{2n-2}{2n-1}p_{n-1}(k)
+\frac1{2n-1}p_{n-1}(k-1).$$
For $n\ge 2$, with $p_1(1)=1$ and $p_n(k)=0$ outside $1\le k\le n$. For example, the probabilities $(p_n(1),p_n(2),\dots,p_n(n))$ for one through $n$ loops are
$$
n=1 : (1), \quad
n=2 : \frac1{3}(2,1),\quad
n=3 : \frac1{15}(8,6,1),\quad
n=4 : \frac1{105}(48,44,12,1).
$$
Does the above recurrence relation admit a closed-form expression for $p_n(k)$ in terms of $n$ and $k$?

Answer A:
Using your notation, $p_n(k)$ is the coefficient of the $z^k$ term in the polynomial $$g_n(z) = \frac{1}{(2n-1)!!} \prod_{j=0}^{n-1} (z + 2j),$$
where $(2n-1)!! = (2n-1)(2n-3) \cdots 3 \cdot 1$ is the double factorial.  While perhaps not a "closed form," it gives a non-recursive method to calculate the probability mass function for any given $n$.  For instance, with $n = 9$, we have
$$\begin{array}{c|c}
k & p_9(k) \\
\hline
1 & \frac{32768}{6435} \\
 2 & \frac{1558528}{225225} \\
 3 & \frac{7559936}{2027025} \\
 4 & \frac{11392}{10725} \\
 5 & \frac{17104}{96525} \\
 6 & \frac{64}{3575} \\
 7 & \frac{8}{7425} \\
 8 & \frac{8}{225225} \\
 9 & \frac{1}{2027025} \\
\end{array}$$

Answer B:
There is a convenient closed form with the Stirling numbers of the first kind. Define the probability generating function
$$P_n(x)=\sum_{k=1}^n p_n(k)x^k$$
Multiplying the recurrence by $x^k$ and sum over $k$ to obtain
$$P_n(x)=\frac{x+2n-2}{2n-1}P_{n-1}(x)$$
With $P_1(x)=x$, iteration gives
$$P_n(x)=\frac{x(x+2)(x+4)\cdots(x+2n-2)}
{1\cdot3\cdot5\cdots(2n-1)}=\frac1{(2n-1)!!}
\sum_{k=1}^n 2^{n-k}\left[{n\atop k}\right]x^k$$

$$\implies p_n(k)=\frac{2^{n-k}}{(2n-1)!!}\left[{n\atop k}\right]$$

Title: Individually Addressed Logical Pauli Measurements by QLDPC Surgery on a Trapped Ion Quantum Computer

Abstract:
Quantum low-density parity check (QLDPC) codes may lead to order-of-magnitude reductions in the qubit overhead required for fault-tolerant quantum computation. Achieving this improved overhead requires logical operations that selectively address individual logical qubits encoded within multi-qubit code blocks. Recently proposed architectures achieve this through QLDPC surgery, in which non-destructive Pauli measurements are performed using ancillary ''gadget'' systems transiently entangled with the code block, generalising lattice surgery. Here we implement QLDPC surgery on a [[10,2,3]] generalised bicycle code using Quantinuum's H2-2 trapped ion processor. A single-round surgery measurement using seven gadget qubits measures the $\bar{X}_1$ operator with a 0.72 [0.32, 1.41]% (95% credible interval) error rate and agrees with subsequent transversal measurement with 1.03 [0.60, 1.65]% error. Decoding across three rounds of syndrome extraction suppresses the gadget measurement error, reducing the error rate to below 0.26%. The syndrome after surgery confirms return to the code space and the unaddressed ''spectator'' qubit is preserved with error 0.21 [0.04, 0.67]% during the three-round measurement. We further demonstrate composition of conjugate basis gadgets by sequentially measuring $\bar{X}_1$ then $\bar{Z}_2$, reusing the gadget qubits, and obtain a 1.12 [0.60, 1.94]% error in the $\bar{Z}_2$ measurement. These results constitute a hardware validation of the generalised surgery primitive underlying Pauli-based computing for QLDPC architectures.

Site: Cs Stack Exchange
Title: Why is there no "reduce-add entire vector" instruction in modern ISAs?
Tags: cpu, instruction-set

Question:
For example, on ARM, the most common reduce add sequence would be:

faddp.4s v0, v0, v0
faddp.2s v0, v0, v0

However, since faddp.4s dest, a, b accepts 2 inputs, and computes dest = [a[0] + a[1], a[2] + a[3], b[0] + b[1], b[2] + b[3]], then doing faddp.4s v0, v0, v0 does redundant ALU ops by adding the same things to themselves twice. On x86 where the common idiom is:

haddps xmm0, xmm0
haddps xmm0, xmm0

The second haddps is even worse, doing 4 adds when you only care about 1. Although the adds are in parallel, doing more than necessary still seems inefficient, e.g., for power consumption, etc.

Therefore, I would expect that adding a dedicated reduce add instruction that takes one vector operand and produces the scalar v[0] + v[1] + v[2] + v[3] right from the get go would be more efficient, however neither of the dominant ISAs (x86, ARM) have that. Though to be fair, x86 has dpps but that only matters if you need to multiply 2 vectors before reduce-adding them.

Is there any particular architectural reason why having a single instruction that reduce-adds an entire vector with no computation performed on "dummy" lanes, is problematic, or was not added?

Site: History Stack Exchange
Title: How were losses to and by German submarines deemed "acceptable" (or not) during World War II?
Tags: world-war-two, nazi-germany, naval, allies

Question:
During the five years of the Battle of the Atlantic, German submarines sank something like 2919 Allied merchant ships while losing 783 of their own vessels, a "kill ratio" of nearly 4 to 1. Although heavily skewed in favor of the Germans, a naive characterization is that this ratio was "acceptable" to the Allies and "unacceptable" to the Germans because the Allies won.

At the height of the battle, in March 1943, the Germans sank 82 Allied merchant ships, for the loss of 12 submarines, a nearly 7 to 1 ratio that was celebrated by the Germans, and caused great consternation from the Allies. The following month, the German submarine loss rose by 1 to 13, but Allied ship losses fell to 39. The Allies cheered, probably because this ratio was "only" 3 to 1. In early May, the tally was something like one submarine to one merchant ship, causing Germany to greatly reduce submarine operations.

Was it "kill ratios" that made relative ship losses acceptable or not? Or was something else at work like replacement capacity? Did "acceptability" measures change over time as the increased production of American Liberty ships changed the overall dynamics of shipping?

Title: Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration for Long-Horizon Tasks

Abstract:
LLM-based agents are increasingly used to complete complex, long-horizon tasks without human intervention. To make progress toward the task goal, agents need to perform different duties, such as planning and verification, when needed. To understand how single agents manage these duties during long-horizon execution, we conduct a preliminary study. Our analysis shows that verification has the strongest association with task success, but often occurs late, leaving limited opportunities for correction. We also find that the proportion of duty-relevant information decreases as records from different duties accumulate in a shared context. These findings lead us to examine whether multi-agent systems (MAS) can address these problems by assigning duties to agents with separate contexts. Our analysis shows that this separation alone is insufficient. Agents can lose track of the overall goal and repeat prior investigations. They may also lack necessary background while receiving irrelevant information from others. To maintain goal awareness and coordinate collaboration as task needs change, we propose Goal-Aware Dynamic Multi-Agent Collaboration (GAD). It uses a growing execution graph to organize subtasks and their dependencies. To keep agents focused on their goals, each context retains the original instruction and the assigned task's goal and acceptance conditions. To adapt collaboration and information sharing during execution, agents can divide tasks into subtasks and specify dependencies based on execution evidence. These dependencies guide when agents work and which results they receive. Verification and recovery check subtask results and full task completion against their goals, providing feedback for repair when checks fail.

Title: RFLocMatch: Reference-Conditioned Residual Learning from Angle-Delay Spectra for Accurate Localization

Abstract:
Radio fingerprint localization supports mobile robots and location-aware services when satellite positioning is unreliable. Angle-delay power fingerprints capture power distributions over angles and delays, but localization remains vulnerable to spatial ambiguity and measurement perturbations. Reflections and blockage can produce similar fingerprints at distant locations, while noise in query fingerprints can alter query-reference rankings despite a clean reference library. These effects can place a distant reference first in the ranking, creating tail errors. Similarity scores can generate plausible candidates, but reliable selection requires candidate-specific residual evidence and comparison across alternatives. This separation motivates RFLocMatch, which uses complementary joint and link-specific matching to preserve candidate locations supported by different links. Reference-conditioned residual learning then scores each candidate using the query and reference fingerprints, their absolute difference, and their element-wise product, while candidate-context modeling compares alternatives. Tail-focused training emphasizes costly errors, and inference replaces the initial match only when a candidate's score advantage exceeds a validation-calibrated threshold. On ray-tracing-generated data, RFLocMatch reduces dual-transmitter 99th-percentile error by 75.2% under link and receiver perturbations relative to the best-performing baseline. On real-world single-transmitter channel impulse response (CIR) measurements with motion-assisted angular-spectrum estimation, it attains 8.25-m 90th-percentile error and 3.83-m mean absolute error.

Title: Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert Review: Application to Online Cell-Type Labeling

Abstract:
Artificial intelligence (AI) models can accelerate cell-type annotation in digital pathology, but safely scaling their use requires determining, with error control, which model-generated labels can be accepted without expert review. This is challenging in evolving workflows because cell morphology and type composition may change across tissue regions and slides, making one-time calibration unreliable. We propose Conformal Annotation with Randomized Expert review under Distribution shift (CARED), a distribution-free framework that leverages randomized expert audit to achieve long-run error control for AI-assisted annotation under distribution shift. For each incoming batch, CARED uniformly selects a subset of cases for expert review and uses the acquired labels to calibrate later decisions. Among unreviewed cases, CARED determines a subset of them to safely skip expert labeling, while suggesting candidate labels for the others for downstream resolution. We prove that this workflow provides long-run control of cumulative error over both the full stream and the cells outside of the audit sample, without stationarity or exchangeability assumptions. We further enhance the framework by introducing class-conditional guarantees to ensure error control within important but rare cell types, together with a utility module to target more automatic resolutions, smaller candidate sets, and greater biological coherence, without compromising validity. Experiments on pancreas, lung, and ovary annotation streams, together with a stream constructed from real expert annotations, show that CARED controls the cumulative errors while a substantial fraction of cells (up to 70%) bypass expert review.

Site: Stats Stack Exchange
Title: If PH assumption is failing when using Cox-PH model, is using Weibull helpful?
Tags: survival, cox-model, weibull-distribution

Question:
I am using survival analysis to analyze unemployment duration from a panel dataset. I would like to control for covariates, and hence I decided to use a Cox PH Model. However, after fitting model, I run the PH test using cox.zph() in R. All my covariates have corresponding p-value of $< 2 \times 10^{-16}$. I tried stratifying using various variables, but that only marginally improves the p-value for some covariates.

I am considering using different models now. I was suggested to use the Weibull model, but I am not sure if this will work as Weibull model also follows the PH assumption. So my questions is:

i) Is there any point trying to use a Weibull model?

ii) What other models should I consider using?

Answer A:
One big advantage of the Cox PH model is that it does not make assumptions about the baseline hazard function, where parametric models do, with the Weibull model assuming the baseline hazard follows a Weibull distribution. Unfortunately, that is an assumption and, if violated, the results can be very misleading.

If you go the parametric route and do not have good substantive reasons to choose one distribution, it is common to try several and choose based on such criteria as AIC.

Other ways of dealing with violation of the PH assumption (including some discussion of when the violation may not matter) are covered in this thread and its subthreads and probably other threads on CV.

Answer B:
Using a Weibull model will not help: as you say, the Weibull model is a proportional hazards model.

It could help to use other accelerated failure models, eg, lognormal. Whether this works will depend on what the failure in proportional hazards looks like.

At one extreme: if all the hazard ratios show a similar pattern of increase or decrease over time then a different underlying model might fix the problem

At the other: if the hazard ratio for some covariates is roughly constant over time but the  hazard ratio for other covariates decreases strongly, changing the underlying model won't help -- you need to model time-dependent effects.  This sort of thing happens fairly frequently in medical data: some measurements get 'stale', so that a year-old measurement of (say) clotting time doesn't tell you much about current risk.  Others don't: if someone was old or low-income or had a history of smoking a year ago, the measurement is still just as valid as it was.

You can look at changes in the hazard ratio over time with smoothed Schoenfeld residuals -- in R, this is survival::plot.cox.zph

Title: Modulo k-orientations of highly edge-connected signed graphs

Abstract:
A modulo $k$-orientation of a signed graph is an orientation in which the outdegree and indegree are congruent modulo $k$ at every vertex. We show that, for every odd integer $k\ge3$, every essentially $k$-unbalanced $(6k-10)$-edge-connected signed graph admits a modulo $k$-orientation. This improves the edge-connectivity bound of Zhu [JCTB, 112 (2015)] from $6k-7$ to $6k-10$.

Title: PolarFlow: Spectral Geometric Flow Matching for Directed Graph Generation via Polar Decomposition

Abstract:
Directed graphs model asymmetric relationships in biology, transportation, social networks, and electronic design automation. Recent discrete diffusion and flow-matching methods generate directed graphs effectively, but their edge-wise categorical formulations require dense predictions over all ordered node pairs and repeated categorical updates during generation. This motivates a fundamental question: can comparable generative quality be achieved through a more computationally efficient formulation that better exploits the structure of directed adjacency matrices? Existing benchmarks also cover limited network structures, restricting comprehensive evaluation. We introduce PolarFlow, a continuous geometric flow-matching framework based on polar decomposition and truncated spectral coordinates. Its representation comprises four coupled components: a Stiefel frame and rotation angles encoding the orthogonal factor, and a second Stiefel frame and nonnegative eigenvalues characterizing the positive-semidefinite factor. PolarFlow learns a joint velocity field along geometry-aware conditional paths on this product space, reconstructs a continuous adjacency-score matrix, and discretizes it into a binary directed graph. By replacing discrete edge-wise generation with joint continuous transport, PolarFlow improves computational efficiency while retaining global adjacency structure. To broaden evaluation, we introduce complementary Circuit and Twitter benchmarks spanning engineered functional and naturally evolved social networks. Across synthetic and real-world datasets, PolarFlow achieves generative quality comparable to competitive discrete methods while substantially reducing training and sampling time.

Title: Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces

Abstract:
We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a Hölder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fréchet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.

Title: What Survives Label Downsampling? Exact Region Survival for Coarse Segmentation Targets

Abstract:
Segmentation networks that predict at an output stride are trained against label maps downsampled by strided sampling, nearest-neighbor resampling or majority pooling. These methods label each coarse grid cell on its own, so a region that wins no cell is absent from the target and receives no positive label. We present MatchDown, which builds the coarse target from a minimum-cost matching between regions and the grid cells they occupy. It keeps as many regions as any one-region-per-cell target can, certifies how many losses are unavoidable, and with priority tiers (MatchDown-P) keeps every evaluated region (a region that a metric scores) of at least one cell's area. On COCO, Cityscapes and BBBC038 at factors 2 to 16, MatchDown-P loses exactly the minimum number of regions, whereas the downsampling used by StarDist, nnU-Net and connectomics pyramids loses four to five times as many on COCO at factor 8. Keeping a region in the target and reconstructing its shape are different problems: we show that no region lost by majority pooling can be reconstructed above IoU 0.5 by upsampling any coarse target, yet on BBBC038 a star-convex head trained on MatchDown targets segments 35% of the nuclei that majority pooling loses above IoU 0.5, against 15% when trained on majority targets and 24% on StarDist's strided target. On two nucleus datasets, with thresholds cross-validated for count error, this head has instance accuracy at IoU 0.5 (Acc50) 2.6 to 4.2 points above the strided target and at most 2.8 points below cell-center sampling, and a lower count error than the strided and cell-center targets on BBBC039. On BBBC039, an affinity head, which outputs one label per cell, lowers count error relative to majority targets by 9.3 nuclei per image at 7.2 points lower Acc50. MatchDown runs once, before training, in place of the label-downsampling step.

	+ \sin ( \theta ) \sqrt{ 1 - \sin^2( \theta ) } \right)  + C \\
%
I &=
	\left( \dfrac{25}{2} \right) \left( \sin^{-1} \left( \dfrac{ x }{5 } \right)

OP’s questions:

We should let $x=5\sin \theta$ for $-\frac{\pi}{2}\le\theta \le \frac{\pi}{2}$ so that sine function is bijective which guarantees the existence of arcsine and $\sqrt{\cos^2 \theta}=\cos \theta. $

Your solution is correct and fine. As @[user] Arbaut said, integration by parts may be faster as below:
$$
\begin{aligned}
I & =x \sqrt{25-x^2}+\int x \frac{x}{\sqrt{25-x^2}} d x \\
& =x \sqrt{25-x^2}+\int \frac{25-\left(25-x^2\right)}{\sqrt{25-x^2}} d x \\
& =x \sqrt{25-x^2}+25 \sin ^{-1} \frac{x}{5}-\int \sqrt{25-x^2} d x \\
I & =\frac{1}{2}\left(x \sqrt{25-x^2}+25\sin^{-1} \frac{x}{5}\right)+C

As to 1, you were given an indefinite integral so there are no limits of integration, and so you should not introduce them. It is good practice to check whether there are any issues with the domain, but in this case it all works out.

Title: Perfect state transfer on unicyclic graphs

Abstract:
We characterize adjacency perfect state transfer in connected unicyclic graphs: the transfer vertices are opposite degree-two vertices of a four-cycle, and the two attached trees satisfy a characteristic-polynomial condition. Except for the four-cycle, the transfer pair is unique and the minimum transfer time is $π/\sqrt2$. Outside the four-cycle, we obtain sharp lower bounds of $46$ on the order and $10$ on the maximum degree, and classify all examples of maximum degree at most $20$. A finite inverse construction enumerates all realizations of a prescribed eigenvalue support at the transfer vertices. For supports of size at least seven, we establish the sharp maximum-degree lower bound of $21$. Every seven-element support $\{0,\pm\sqrt2,\pm u\sqrt2,\pm v\sqrt2\}$, with odd integers $3\leq u<v$, is realizable, and every such realization has attachment depth at most four. Explicit branching rules give a minimum-order recurrence. Among all connected unicyclic graphs admitting perfect state transfer with seven-element eigenvalue support, the minimum order is $218$, attained uniquely up to isomorphism.

Title: Scotland rail stations without car access
Tags: trains, scotland

Question:
The Scotrail website says on their route maps page:

Taking the train is one of the best ways to enjoy our country's stunning landscapes, with some places only accessible by rail.

A random selection of a dozen or so stations from the map didn't turn anything up, so I'm curious if anyone knows which "places" they're referring to.

Answer A:
It does not say 'towns' or 'villages' or 'stations' not accessible by road, but places, i.e. "our country's stunning landscapes", some of which can only be seen from a train, not from a road.

The sentence

Taking the train is one of the best ways to enjoy our country's stunning landscapes, with some places only accessible by rail.

reads as better English by not switching the topic at the comma, from landscapes to stations. Places has a very broad definition, and Merriam-Webster includes 'physical surroundings' and 'an indefinite region or expanse' among others. So here it should be obvious that it refers to the subject 'landscapes'. On the other hand, a sentence which suddenly switches its meaning to refer to some isolated stations, is very clunky.

Also, there is a particular modern use of accessible – somewhere is accessible if it can be accessed by walkers, cycles, buggies and wheelchairs – everyone.

The line from Tulloch Station to Rannoch Station (passing through Corrour) runs for about 20 miles through spectacular scenery with no public roads. For the general public to enjoy this scenery, they have to go by train.

It is just advertising copy, anyway.

Answer B:
Starting a list of candidates as Community Wiki, which people may be able to confirm or refute with further research.  Feel free to add to this!

Corrour station is "accessible by rail only" in the sense that there is no public road access (but access via a private road is possible).  (Credit B. Liu)

Altnabreac is described by a 2025 BBC article as "10 miles from the nearest road", though there do appear to be unpaved roads or tracks reaching it.  Wikipedia says it is on a private dirt road, and is 6.8 miles from the nearest paved road.

Title: Cross-Controller Transfer via In-Context Behavior Adaptation

Abstract:
Generalist robot policies increasingly learn from data collected across diverse tasks and embodiments, yet typically assume a single controller for each robot. This assumption limits transfer because different controllers can assign different physical meanings to the same action and may require different strategies to complete a task. We study how to transfer robot data across both embodiments and controllers without allowing conflicting action interpretations to interfere with learning. Our setting spans six controller types as well as variations in controller gains and compliance. We propose a framework that encodes behavioral interaction under a controller through examples of commanded actions and the resulting robot motions. A transformer context encoder summarizes these interactions, allowing a single policy to adapt in context. Across real-world experiments, our method improves average success by 33 percentage points over naive data pooling, achieves 50\% success on unseen controller modes and 52\% on unseen controller gains, and transfers to tasks with limited controller-specific data. On contact-rich tasks such as USB insertion and surface wiping, behavioral interaction context enables the policy to adapt not only its actions but also its strategy. Our results provide a path toward generalist robot policies that can leverage data collected across diverse action interpretations. For more information, visit \href{https://controller-transfer.github.io}{https://controller-transfer.github.io}.

Title: Comparative Evaluation of LLM-Based Review Paradigms for Academic Paper Quality Assessment

Abstract:
Growing submission volumes have renewed interest in using large language models (LLMs) to support peer review. It remains unclear how such evaluation should be structured, how much the model matters, and whether LLM scores predict research impact. We evaluate five paradigms across three input representations and three LLMs on 232 stratified ICLR 2025 submissions. Direct absolute rating matches comparative ranking on rank correlation with human scores, yet compresses most predictions above the accept threshold, flagging almost none of the papers reviewers scored below it. A base-rate-matched recalibration control locates the cause: comparative ranking supplies placement, not better ordering, and after recalibration Direct Rating reaches higher agreement than Elo while making 24% as many API calls. Abstract-only input beats full-paper summarization, and model choice matters as much as paradigm choice. Replicating on all 11,513 scored submissions reproduces these patterns, shows absolute agreement depends on the evaluated set's score spread, and finds none beating an always-reject baseline in accuracy. Human scores track citations better than any paradigm, with one exception: Group Rating retains its citation correlation after controlling for human scores, and alone ranks within the accepted pool. Ranking quality alone cannot assess review quality; calibration, thresholds, model, and target outcome all matter.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Connected graph with diameter at least three has connected complement
Tags: graph-theory, solution-verification, soft-question, first-order-logic

Question:
I came across this problem in the book Combinatorics and Graph Theory.

Prove that if $G$ is connected and $\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}(G) \geq3$, then $\overline{G}$ is connected.

Simple enough. Here is the proof I came up with:

We use contrapositive and the fact that $\overline{\overline{G}}=G$. Suppose $G$ is disconnected. Consider any two vertices $u,v\in V(G)=V(\overline{G})$. Either $u$ and $v$ are in the same component or in distinct components. In the latter case, there is an edge $uv$ in $\overline{G}$, so $d_{\overline{G}}(u,v)=1$. In the former case, pick any vertex $w$ in another component of $G$. There are edges $uw$ and $vw$ in $\overline{G}$, so $d(u,v)\leq 2$. In either case, $d(u,v)<3$.

But I have a slight issue with this proof. Let $A(G)$ be the statement (predicate) "$G$ is connected", let $B(G)$ be "$\mathop{\mathrm{diam}}(G) \geq3$", and let $C(G)$ be "$\overline{G}$ is connected". We are required to prove that $$[A(G)\land B(G)]\implies C(G).$$
The contrapositive is that $$\lnot C(G)\implies [\lnot A(G)\lor \lnot B(G)].$$
What I proved is $\lnot C(G)\implies \lnot B(G)$. Is there something wrong in what I am doing? I do not like this redundancy in a statement as simple as this.

Thank you.

Draft text:
Nathaniel "Nate" Jacobs is a fictional character in the American teen drama television series Euphoria, created by Sam Levinson. He is portrayed by Jacob Elordi, with Gabriel Golub portraying a younger version of the character. Nate is introduced as a high school football player and the eldest son of Cal and Marsha Jacobs. He is characterized by his volatile temperament, controlling behavior, and preoccupation with masculinity and social status. His relationship with his father, whose secret sexual life he discovers as a child, becomes a central part of his character. [ref: Sam Levinson on Euphoria, Television Academy]

Nate's major storylines include his relationships with Maddy Perez, Jules Vaughn, and Cassie Howard, as well as his increasingly antagonistic relationship with Cal. He manipulates Jules under the alias "Tyler" after discovering her sexual encounter with his father, and later begins a relationship with Cassie while she is Maddy's close friend. Five years after graduating from high school, Nate is married to Cassie and becomes involved in his father's real-estate business. His financial difficulties lead to his involvement with loan sharks, who eventually kill him. [ref: 'Euphoria' Season 3 Episode 7 Recap: Nate Jacobs Dies, [[Variety (magazine)]

==Background==

Nate is the eldest son of Cal and Marsha Jacobs and grows up in East Highland, California. His father places considerable emphasis on physical strength, athletic achievement, and conventional masculinity during his childhood. Nate has a younger brother, Aaron, and an older brother, Derek, who dies before the events of the series.

At the age of 11, Nate discovers a collection of videos documenting Cal's sexual encounters with men and transgender women. The discovery profoundly affects his perception of his father and contributes to his later preoccupation with masculinity and sexuality. Sam Levinson has described Nate, alongside several other characters, as coming from a troubled home and attempting to fill emotional voids through sex, drugs, and adrenaline.

As a teenager, Nate becomes a star football player at East Highland High School. He develops a reputation for aggression and intimidation and begins an unstable relationship with Maddy Perez. Their relationship is repeatedly disrupted by jealousy, possessiveness, and violence.

Nate later discovers that Maddy possesses intimate photographs of Jules Vaughn and learns that Jules previously had a sexual encounter with Cal. Using the online identity "Tyler", Nate begins communicating with Jules and develops an emotional attachment to her while concealing his identity. After learning that Jules has evidence of his father's encounter with her, Nate threatens to expose her private photographs unless she remains silent.

During his senior year, Nate begins a secret relationship with Cassie Howard, despite her friendship with Maddy. Their relationship becomes public after Maddy discovers the affair and contributes to the breakdown of Cassie's friendship with her.

Following high school, Nate takes over his father's real-estate business and marries Cassie. Five years after the events of the second season, he experiences financial difficulties and becomes indebted to loan sharks. After being abducted and buried alive, Nate is rescued but subsequently killed by the men pursuing him. His death occurs in the seventh episode of the third season, "Rain or Shine".

==Personality==

Nate is portrayed as confident, physically imposing, and highly competitive, particularly in relation to football and his social position at school. He maintains a controlled outward appearance while frequently responding to perceived threats or challenges with anger and intimidation. His behavior toward his romantic partners is characterized by possessiveness, jealousy, manipulation, and violence.

A significant aspect of Nate's characterization is his relationship with masculinity. His father's emphasis on physical strength and traditional masculine behavior contributes to Nate's efforts to construct a similarly dominant public persona. His discovery of Cal's sexual encounters creates a conflict between his understanding of masculinity and the reality of his father's private life. Levinson has described Nate as one of several Euphoria characters who attempt to compensate for emotional difficulties through sex, drugs, or adrenaline.

Elordi has described Nate as a deeply conflicted character whose anger provides an outlet for problems he does not know how to confront directly. He has also characterized the role as substantially more complex than the version of Nate presented in the initial audition material, which he described as a stereotypical aggressive jock. [ref: Jacob Elordi Called Nate in "Euphoria" an "Emotional Terrorist", Teen Vogue]

Nate's relationships with Maddy, Jules, and Cassie each expose different aspects of his personality. His relationship with Maddy is marked by possessiveness and physical violence, while his relationship with Jules develops through an anonymous online identity that allows him to express feelings he is unwilling to acknowledge publicly. His relationship with Cassie similarly reflects his desire for control and his difficulty separating intimacy from possession.

Title: Hopf Algebra of Graphs for Operator Splitting Methods

Abstract:
Motivated by combinatorial identities arising in the study of operator splitting methods and their description in terms of bipartite rooted trees, we establish a connection between operator splitting methods and the theory of combinatorial Hopf algebras. We show that the inclusion-exclusion expansion of the elementary weight of a rooted tree over its rooted subforests can be interpreted as the antipode of Schmitt's Hopf algebra of graphs. This interpretation recovers known identities for operator splitting and partitioned Runge-Kutta methods from general properties of the antipode. We further show that adjoint operator splitting methods can be described algebraically through the antipode and the canonical involution of the original method. The resulting framework also yields new combinatorial identities and connects the analysis of geometric numerical integrators with the theory of incidence Hopf algebras.

Title: Archimedean Asai Zeta Integrals and Cohomological Test Vectors

Abstract:
We construct explicit test vectors in the minimal $U(n)$-types of cohomological principal series representations of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb C)$, together with Schwartz functions, for which the Flicker zeta integrals equal the corresponding Asai $L$-factors. Both the vectors and the Schwartz functions are independent of $s$, with all normalization constants given explicitly. We construct the vectors through a polynomial realization of Schur modules. Schur orthogonality reduces the Flicker integrals to Mellin transforms of Whittaker functions, and Godement sections yield a recurrence for their Jacquet integrals. The lower-rank vectors depend on the remaining integration variables, preventing a direct reduction to lower-rank Flicker integrals. We overcome this difficulty by combining growth estimates derived from the recurrence with the Asai functional equation. This proves that the holomorphic quotient of the Flicker integral by its Asai $L$-factor is constant. An explicit asymptotic calculation shows that this constant is exactly one.

Title: ChatGPT as a Surveillance Assistant? An Exploratory Case Study of AI-Assisted Surveillance Risks

Abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) can generate detailed guidance, functional code, and persuasive text at scale. As one of the most widely used consumer language model products as of 2026, ChatGPT gives broad public access to these capabilities, motivating concerns about its potential use in surveillance-related tasks. We present an exploratory case study of what potentially harmful surveillance assistance looks like in ChatGPT's public web interface. We contribute a taxonomy of seven surveillance risk categories based on prior LLM risk research and reports of deployed surveillance systems, instantiated as 110 prompts, along with a manually reviewed analysis of ChatGPT's responses. Prompts were issued using two approaches: 55 jailbreak prompts drawing on five types of elicitation strategies, and 55 plain-language direct prompts, each run alone, and if unsuccessful, again with a short fixed prefix. We find that ChatGPT provides substantive surveillance guidance for 40 of the 55 jailbreak prompts and for 33 of the 55 direct prompts without any prefix. Compliant responses also rarely included policy mentions or suggestions for privacy-preserving alternatives. We manually review every response and find that even when ChatGPT states a refusal, it may still supply detailed instructions, working code, or architectural guidance alongside brief ethical caveats.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Rhinoceros dolphin

Draft text:
The rhinoceros dolphin (Delphinus rhinoceros) is an alleged species of dolphin first discovered by French naval surgeons Jean René Constant Quoy and Joseph Paul Gaimard on the 19th of October, 1819, in the Pacific ocean while sailing between the Sandwich Islands (now the Hawaiian Islands) and New South Wales, Australia (5°28' N). [ref: Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, Pillet Aîné, Printer-Bookseller, Rue Christine] It was formally described in Voyage Autour de Monde, Fait Par Ordere du Roi, a compendium of the scientific observations and accounts of the Uranie voyage around the world under the rule of Louis de Freycinet in 1824. The species is widely considered dubious. [ref: Delphinus rhinoceros, Quoy & Gaimard, 1824, World Cetacea Database]

== Morphology and discovery ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was described to have been dark in overall colour with sporadic white blotching along the dorsum which ceased around or soon after the dorsal fin closest to the fluke. The first dorsal fin was located close to or on the neck, and the species' head and face were not visible due to a hesitance to breach, a detail noted as being unlike the other dolphins encountered on the voyage. During interactions with the Uranie, the dolphins passed close to the prow of the vessel, though they did not surface frequently enough to be photographed. Consequently, the morphology of any potential beak or snout, was impossible to deduce. The cetaceans were encountered in a pod [ref: Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, ABC-CLIO] and individuals were said to have been double the length of a porpoise. Though the specific species of porpoise being referenced is not mentioned, if the size comparison was made in reference to the common porpoise (Phocoena phocoena), the rhinoceros dolphin would measure close to 3m (10ft) in length. Another two dorsal-finned cetacean resembling a dolphin was sighted breaching and playing amongst common dolphins (Delphinus delphinus) off Lantivet Bay, Cornwall, Wales, in April of 1856 by British naturalist Johnathan Couch who claimed them to have been a maximum of 2.4m (8ft) in length.

== Taxonomy and naming ==
The rhinoceros dolphin was named in reference to its frontal dorsal fin, a defining structure located close to or on the neck in superficial resemblence to the horn of a rhinoceros. [ref: The Natural History of the Ordinary Cetacea or Whales, Lizars] The species is not known from a type specimen or holotype, and is widely considered to be dubious altogether due to a lack of evidence supporting its existence beyond the description by Quoy and Gaimard. Upon description, Quoy and Gaimard suggested the taxonomic classification; (Delphinus rhinoceros), placing the species in the same genus as the common dolphin, though this conclusion was founded on little evidence. [ref: Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, Aquatic Mammals]

Later revisions of the taxonomy of the rhinoceros dolphin by French naturalist René Lesson in his 1828 book, Historie Naturelle Mammiferes place the species instead in the genus (Oxypterus). [ref: Historie Naturelle des Animaux Rares, Baudouin Brothers] This genus had been previously used by French naturalist and polymath Constantine Samuel Rafinesque in 1814 to refer to a large odotocete characterised by possessing two dorsal fins that had stranded itself 10km (6.2 miles) off Licata, Sicily in the September of 1741, which he had classified as O. mongitore. This specimen was said to have measured 13.2m (45ft) in length with a forked tail, a hole in its head that was leaking water, and a mouth equipped with strong teeth by Italian presbyter Antonio Mongitore, who illustrated the specimen along with two other whales, D. dalippus and Physeter urganantus. [ref: "Monstri Marini": Constantine S. Rafinesque's names for three of Antonio Montigore's Sicillian Whales, Archives of Natural History] Lesson refers to Oxypterus as a "subgenus" that he only gives serious attention to at all in light of the rhinoceros dolphin account. In Cetaceans with two dorsal fins, an article published as part of the seventeeth volume of the Aquatic Mammals journal in 1991, Michel Raynal dismissed this account as a misidentified basking shark (Cetorhinus maximus) rather than a newly undiscovered species of Mediterranean two dorsal-finned cetacean akin to the rhinoceros dolphin. Within the same article, Raynal proposed the hypothetical binomial name for the rhinoceros dolphin; (Cetodipterus rhinoceros), constituting a new genus within the family Delphinidae.

== Consensus in scientific literarure ==

=== In cryptozoology ===
Contemporary discussions of the rhinoceros dolphin occassionally refer to the species as a cryptid, an animal yet to be scientifically recognised due to a lack of substatiated evidence of its existence. It appeared in George M. Eberhart's 2002 book Mysterious Creatures: A Guide to Cryptozoology, where he described it as an "Unknown cetacean of the North Pacific Ocean" and discussed it alongside Couch's account of the two dorsal-finned dolphin spotted off Cornwall.
[truncated]

Draft text:
Kelley Anne Dennison is an American political candidate, licensed massage therapist, small-business owner, and activist from Colorado.She became the Republican nominee for Colorado's 2nd congressional district int he 2026 United States House of Representatives election.Her campaign has focused on economic affordability, environmental conservation, family policy, education reform, and constitutional rights.

== Early life and education ==
Dennison is a Colorado native who has described growing up in a family where political issues andpublicaffairs were openly discussed. According to her campaign interviews, her interest in politicsdevelopedpartly through high school civics and history classes and concerns about the rising cost of living.

She attended Estes Park High School and completed professional training in massage therapy at the Academy of Natural Therapy, receiving a certificate in 2023.

== Career ==

=== Business and massage therapy ===
Before entering electoral politics, Dennison worked as a licensed massage therapist and small-business owner. Her professional background includes operating Wind Bear Holistic Healing, abusiness associated with massage and holistic wellness services.

She has presented her experience working directly with clients and running a small business as a basis for understanding the financial pressures faced by ordinary workers, families, and entrepreneurs.

=== Entry into politics ===
Dennison's first reported involvement in electoral politics included working as a campaign staffer for Republican congressional candidate Adam DeRito. She subsequently decided to run for Congress herself,citing concerns about affordability, government accountability,and the limited participationof younger Americans in politics.

Her candidacy attracted attention because she entered a high-profile congressional race withouthaving previously held elected public office.

== Political career ==

=== 2026 congressional campaign ===
In 2026, Dennison sought the Republican nomination for Colorado's2nd congressional district. She won the Republican primary on June 30, 2026, defeating Christina Blunt and becoming the party's nominee for the general election against Democratic incumbent Joe Neguse.

The race drew attention because the district had historically favoured Democrats. In the 2024 election, Neguse won nearly 70% of the vote, making Dennison's campaign a challenge in a district where Republicans faced a significant electoral disadvantage.

Dennison promoted a grassroots campaign aimed at engaging younger voters and residents of Colorado's mountain communities. She also advocated for greater participation by members of Generation Z in political life.

== Political positions ==
Dennison's campaign platform includes several major policy areas. The following summarizes positions she has publicly expressed; it does not imply that the proposals have been enacted.

=== Economic affordability ===
Dennison has advocated increasing the supply of housing, reducing regulations that she believes increase construction costs, and limiting large corporate investors' purchases of starter homes. Shehas also emphasized the cost of living for working families and younger Coloradans.

=== Environmental conservation ===
She supports responsible land use, conservation of forests and headwater ecosystems, and protection of watersheds. She has also emphasized the relationship between environmental stewardship, water security, and Colorado's outdoor recreation economy.

=== Family and education policy ===
Her campaign supports pro-family policies, greater parental involvement in education, and efforts to improve educational quality and practical career preparation. She also identifies veterans and senior citizens as groups deserving stronger support.

=== Constitutional rights and term limits ===
Dennison supports Second Amendment rights and has signed the U.S. Term Limits pledge, committing to support a constitutional amendment limiting congressional service. Her campaign frames these positions around individual liberty and government accountability.

=== Immigration and government accountability ===
She supports secure borders, enforcement of immigration laws, and more efficient legal immigration pathways. She has also called for greater transparency in government and cooperation across party lines.

== Public image and political significance ==
Dennison has been described in media coverage as an unconventional, younger Republican candidate. Her candidacy combines conservative positions on gun rights and government regulation with an emphasis on housing affordability, environmental conservation, and outreach to younger voters.

Her background as a small-business owner rather than a career politician has been a prominent part of her campaign identity. She has argued that ordinary citizens should participate more actively in public affairs instead of leaving political leadership exclusively to established politicians.

== Electoral status ==
As of October 18, 2026, Dennison is the Republican nominee in the 2026 general election for Colorado's 2nd congressional district.

Site: Money Stack Exchange
Title: Does an EU ISIN lookup/standard exist that explains brokers decisions in protecting inexperienced customers?
Tags: etf, germany, european-union, online-brokerage

Question:
After registering with an online broker and answering a short questionnaire to clarify my "investor profile" (selected zero experience) I placed my first order for an ETF identified as LU0292105359. Opened up the form again for some other ETF, noticed something odd in the fee preview and could have, but chose not to proceed. Eventually I tried to put in a buy order for yet another ETF, this time DE000ETFL342. No order preview this time. Instead, a red message instructed me to update my investor profile before they would accept an order for that, suggesting that this particular product might be unsuitable for me.

Unfortunately, they were a little too helpful in highlighting the buttons to click that lift this protection within seconds. After changing my selection from never having traded at all to having executed a trade before, they were now happy to let me buy DE000ETFL342. Without me being any wiser about what this mechanism was trying to point out, and why it would kick in for one ETF but not the other.

both trading in EUR, UCITS, attempt replication of somewhat popular index, existed for >10y, accumulating, subject to 2019/2088 disclosures, claim in 1286/2014 key information document that risk category is 4/7 and suggest this is a product one would buy and hold onto for years.. sounds like the same general category, no?

Were they trying to protect me from burning money on an unusually expensive passive fund? Trying to shield me from exposure to unhedged USD/EUR risks? Or one fund failing to achieve using derivatives what the other achieves by physically holding index components? Or something else altogether? Well, once I find out which one it was in this case, I will still likely do the same mistake again in the future - thinking two products are very similar in complexity and risk profile, while my broker could determine in a fully automatic lookup that they are not.

Is there an (ideally EU-wide) standard / ISIN lookup that spits out not merely the 1 through 7 risk category I already have, but provides this separate "investor suitability" determination that brokers use to tier products? I would like to keep making use of this protection, even after my broker no longer refuses (at least one additional tier - the protection is still in place for other/higher categories, e.g. I can trigger it on purpose by selecting an option). If there even is such a thing - I understand the answer to this question might be "No, every broker decides based on their own internal criteria."

Related: (US) How to compare "block lists" for brokerages?

Title: Strong-Field-Driven Non-Linear Vibronic Coupling in an Asymmetric Donor-Acceptor Oligomer

Abstract:
Understanding how nuclear motion couples to intramolecular charge transfer beyond the perturbative regime of light--matter interaction remains an open problem. We tackle this problem by investigating the electron-nuclear response of an acceptor-donor-acceptor oligomer with structural asymmetry due to the partial fluorination of an acceptor unit. Adopting real-time time-dependent density functional theory combined with Ehrenfest dynamics, we excite the systems with a resonant pulse of varying intensity, spanning the weak-, intermediate-, and strong-coupling regimes. When nuclei are clamped, field-driven charge preferentially flows from the donor to the fluorinated acceptor, with selectivity reduced upon increasing intensity. With moving ions, the early-time spatial response remains qualitatively unchanged, despite a distinct, spatially asymmetric charge redistribution. In the strong-field regime, nuclear motion preserves the preference for field-driven charge accumulation on the fluorinated acceptor, although the process takes approximately twice the time as in the fixed-nuclei scenario. Mode-resolved kinetic-energy analysis reveals that, with increasing field strength, the laser-induced nuclear response shifts from selected bond stretchings to collective low-frequency modes. These results provide a benchmark for assessing the interplay between vibronic dynamics and strong-field coupling in donor/acceptor oligomers.

state.text:
Title: The asymptotic number of zonotopes

Abstract:
We provide a sharp estimate for the asymptotic number of lattice zonotopes inscribed in [0, n] d as n tends to infinity. Our estimate refines the logarithmic equivalent established by B{á}r{á}ny, Bureaux, and Lund when the sum of the generators of the zonotope is prescribed. As we shall see, the exponential part of our estimate is a polynomial of degree d in n 1/(d+1) , plus a term involving the non-trivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function. Our analysis is based on a correspondence between power sums over primitive vectors (vectors with coprime coordinates) and Eulerian polynomials. We also analyse some combinatorial properties of lattice zonotopes. In particular, we compute the asymptotic mean and variance of the diameter of the graph of a random lattice zonotope inscribed in [0, n] d as n goes to infinity, and show that this diameter satisfies a central limit theorem.

> Every time I key up on 15 meters, the neighbor's TV shows herringbone
> lines and my own PC speakers start buzzing. She says I'm ruining her
> cable. Do I need a new rig?

No, your rig is probably fine. Both symptoms are classic fundamental overload, not spurious emissions. The TV front end and the unshielded speaker amplifier are acting as detectors for a strong signal they were never designed to reject. Put a high-pass filter on her antenna input, wind the speaker leads several turns through a type 43 ferrite toroid, and add a 0.01 uF bypass cap across the amplifier input. If the herringbone persists with the high-pass in, check your own low-pass filter and your station ground.

At 100 watts you are nowhere near the power level that would damage either device."

state.text:
Title: Noise Propagation and Effective Channels in Encrypted Quantum Cloning

Abstract:
We investigate noise propagation in encrypted quantum cloning by formulating the protocol in terms of effective recovery channels. For local single-qubit completely positive trace-preserving noise, a Pauli-basis expansion of the Kraus operators reveals a strong dependence on the location of the physical channel. Noise on an auxiliary signal qubit leaves the reduced recovered state unchanged, whereas noise on an auxiliary key qubit induces a Pauli-diagonal effective channel on the recovered qubit. For the core qubits, the error propagation additionally depends on the parity of the number of entangled pairs. In particular, for noise on the core key qubit with odd parity, distinct physical Pauli sectors merge into the same effective sector, converting isotropic depolarizing noise into an anisotropic recovery channel. We also relate Werner-type resource imperfections to local depolarizing noise and distinguish distributed product depolarization from genuine global depolarization. The results demonstrate that the effective recovery noise is governed not only by noise strength, but also by its physical location and by the structure of the encryption-decryption protocol.

Title: When are complements and substitutes dual?

Abstract:
For binary-action games on bipartite networks, strategic complements and strategic substitutes are one and the same: each can be transformed into the other by relabelling the actions of every player on exactly one side. In this note, I show that bipartiteness is necessary and sufficient for such a relabelling; as a consequence, bipartite networks are precisely those on which every binary-action game with strategic substitutes must have a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium.

state.text:
Title: The S-function at arbitrary order: hyperplanes of symmetries and the realisability condition

Abstract:
For a scalar equation $y^{(n)}=\varphi(x,y,\dots,y^{(n-1)})$ the $S$-function of the extended Prelle--Singer method is a vector $S=(S_0,\dots,S_{n-2})$, the null-form vector of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Lakshmanan and collaborators, and the jet gradient of a first integral solves the adjoint of the variational equation. We describe the solutions of the system satisfied by $S$ intrinsically, and determine which of them come from first integrals. Over the field $C$ of first integrals the solutions are exactly the hyperplanes of the $n$-dimensional space $VV$ of symmetry characteristics, recovered from $n-1$ independent characteristics by a Plücker formula; in flow-box coordinates they are the hyperplane fields on the local space of leaves. A solution is the $S$-vector of a first integral if and only if the corresponding hyperplane field is integrable. This Frobenius condition splits into the $S$-system itself plus $\binom n3$ further differential conditions, so it is vacuous for $n=2$ and a genuine restriction for every $n\ge3$, for which we give an explicit non-realisable solution. The same picture explains why $λ$-symmetries and $S$-functions coincide only when $n=2$: line fields and hyperplane fields agree only on surfaces. For the computation of $S$ we record that the system is equivalent to one scalar equation for the last component, which is the Riccati form of the adjoint variational equation, and we spell out what this does and does not imply for a rational search.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type

Draft text:
----

Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo–Campeau type (SEMDGC) is an inherited skeletal dysplasia associated with pathogenic variants in ERI1. It causes pronounced short stature and abnormalities affecting the spine, pelvis, hips, and limbs. Fingers or toes may be shortened, underdeveloped, or absent, and facial features vary between affected individuals. [ref: Spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia, Guo-Campeau type (Concept ID: C5882737), MedGen] The disorder follows an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. [ref: ERI1, PanelApp]

== Signs and symptoms ==
Skeletal manifestations include limb shortening and abnormalities of the hands and feet. Reported findings include short digits, joined digits, curved fingers, absent toes, restricted elbow extension, and dislocation of the radial head. Hydronephrosis and vesicoureteral reflux have also been recorded.

Radiographs show flattened vertebral bodies, irregular vertebral endplates, and scoliosis in affected individuals. Severity varies: two siblings are alive into their twenties, whereas three other individuals with the severe skeletal phenotype died in infancy or early childhood. These observations describe the initial series rather than an established survival estimate. [ref: Null and missense mutations of ERI1 cause a recessive phenotypic dichotomy in humans, The American Journal of Human Genetics]

== Genetics ==
ERI1 is located on chromosome 8p23.1. It encodes a 3′-to-5′ exoribonuclease involved in RNA processing. Reported severe cases have carried at least one pathogenic missense variant. By contrast, individuals with two null alleles have generally shown milder skeletal involvement. [ref: Congenital Bone Disorders Associated with ERI1-Mediated RNA Metabolism Dysfunction: Spondylo-Epi-Metaphyseal Dysplasia Guo-Campeau Type and Beyond, Current Osteoporosis Reports] The latter presentation, involving digital abnormalities and mild intellectual disability, is classified separately as Hoxha–Aliu syndrome (OMIM 620662).

== Diagnosis ==
The original study combined clinical and radiographic assessment with exome or genome sequencing. Candidate variants were investigated by Sanger sequencing and where parental samples were available, family studies.

== History ==
Guo and colleagues described the disorder in 2023. Their study included eight individuals from seven families with ERI1 variants; five individuals from four families had the severe skeletal phenotype.
==Research==
Cell experiments linked the missense variants to impaired exonuclease activity, abnormal 5.8S ribosomal RNA processing, and reduced histone messenger RNA degradation. Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells also showed impaired cartilage differentiation.

A 2025 review emphasized that the mechanism connecting altered RNA metabolism to the skeletal abnormalities remains incompletely understood. It also noted that Eri1-knockout mice do not reproduce the full human phenotype, limiting their usefulness as a model of the severe disorder.

== References ==

Site: Law Stack Exchange
Title: Does codifying evidence law freeze privilege categories and block new ones from developing?
Tags: common-law, evidence, comparative-law, comparative

Question:
I have been reading about privilege doctrines across common law jurisdictions and am trying to understand a structural difference.

In England, litigation privilege (protecting communications with third parties made for the dominant purpose of preparing for litigation) developed as a distinct common law rule, separate from legal advice privilege (protecting lawyer-client communications). Both are recognized as subcategories of legal professional privilege.

In India, the evidence law was codified in 1872 as the Indian Evidence Act, with specific statutory provisions on legal professional privilege (ss. 126-129). However, there appears to be no statutory provision for litigation privilege. A recent academic study (Upadhyay, 2024, in The International Journal of Evidence & Proof) argues this is because the doctrine was still forming in English courts at the time of codification and was missed by the drafters.
My question: In jurisdictions that codified their evidence rules (India, Singapore, etc.) versus those that left privilege to common law development (England, Canada), how has this structural difference affected the scope of privilege available to litigants? Specifically, can a codified evidence system accommodate new privilege categories without legislative amendment, or does codification inherently create a "freezing" effect?

I am particularly interested in whether courts in codified jurisdictions have found workarounds, and if so, whether those workarounds have been legally sound.
