Title: Could a Black Hole Eventually Become a White Hole in a Separate Universe?
Tags: black-holes, white-holes

Question:
I’ve been thinking about a theoretical possibility involving black holes, white holes, and the creation of new universes, and I’d like to know whether anything like this is compatible with current physics.

My idea is that when a black hole forms, spacetime inside it continues to stretch or evolve under extreme gravitational conditions. Could there be some physical limit at which this process can no longer continue, causing a transition rather than a singularity?

In this hypothetical scenario, that transition could produce a white-hole-like region in a separate universe. From the perspective of an observer in the original universe, the object would still appear to be a black hole, while the other side of the transition would lead to a new, expanding spacetime.

The new universe might experience something analogous to its own Big Bang. If the process were possible, could every black hole potentially give rise to a separate universe, each with its own cosmic evolution and eventually its own black holes?

I’m particularly curious about three questions:

Spacetime and the interior: Is there any physical basis for thinking that the extreme curvature or evolution of spacetime inside a black hole could reach a limit that prevents a classical singularity from forming?

Black-hole-to-white-hole transitions: Do any existing quantum-gravity theories allow a black hole to transition into a white hole or connect to a separate, expanding universe?

Baby universes and the Big Bang: Could such a transition plausibly produce a causally disconnected universe whose expansion resembles a Big Bang to observers inside it?

I realize that spacetime may not literally stretch or tear like a material fabric, and that this is speculative. I’m interested in whether there is an existing theory that resembles this idea, what the major physical obstacles would be, and what evidence or mathematical conditions would be needed to make it viable.

Is this concept related to existing research on quantum bounces, black-hole cosmology, or baby universes? If so, which papers or theories would be the best starting point?

I’m not proposing that this is how black holes actually work. I’m curious whether the underlying mechanism is physically possible.

Priyalal Sirisena (born 25 May 1979) is a Sri Lankan attorney-at-law, human rights lawyer, and novelist. == Early life and education ==
Sirisena was born on 25 May 1979 in Kurunegala, Sri Lanka. He studied law at the University of Colombo, graduating with a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) in 2006, and was admitted to the bar as an Attorney-at-Law of the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka. He later earned a Master of Laws (LL.M.) from the same university.

== Legal career ==
Sirisena works on legal cases involving fundamental rights, police misconduct, and custodial torture in Sri Lanka. He has contributed to civil society reports submitted for Sri Lanka's Universal Periodic Review at the United Nations.

In June 2018, Sirisena filed a Fundamental Rights petition in the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka against police officers, alleging interference with his duties as legal counsel. [ref: Lawyer sues cops for stifling his professional rights, Daily Mirror] In May 2023, Front Line Defenders reported that Sirisena faced threats and intimidation related to his legal work in Kurunegala.

== Literary work ==
Sirisena worked as a journalist for The Island newspaper before writing fiction. He authored the Sinhala novel Deyyange Atha (The Elephant of the Gods), published by Vidarshana Publishers. [ref: Deiyange Etha by Priyalal Sirisena, Katha.lk] The book was shortlisted for the Swarna Pusthaka Awards in 2025.

Title: Fock Projections between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Spaces: Full-Range Boundedness and Compactness

Abstract:
The Fock--Bargmann projection \(P_t\) is initially an orthogonal projection on a Gaussian Hilbert space. We characterize the boundedness and compactness of \[ P_t:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal F_β^{p_2,q_2} \] and of its associated maximal projection \[ P_t^+:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow L_β^{p_2,q_2} \] for all \(t,α,β>0\) and \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2\le\infty\). Set \[ Δ(t;α,β):=t^2-2βt+αβ, \qquad d(p,q):=\frac1q-\frac1p. \] For both operators, boundedness holds exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with \[ q_1\le q_2, \qquad d(p_2,q_2)\le d(p_1,q_1). \] Both operators are compact exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with both of the above boundary inequalities strict. Thus boundedness forces the source exponents into the Banach range, whereas when \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), every target exponent is admissible, including quasi-Banach ones. Annular discretization reduces the problem to drifted Gaussian sequence operators, whose comparison with diagonal sequence operators yields the endpoint criteria and quantitative tail estimates. A dilation--multiplier transfer gives corresponding results for Gaussian-twisted Fock operators, including Berezin transforms.

Title: Learning Latent Fields in Multiobject Tracking

Abstract:
Multiobject tracking using measurements from ar- rays of wireless sensors is a key task in applications ranging from autonomous navigation to public safety. Many existing methods compress raw complex-valued signals into detections or intensity maps during preprocessing, thereby discarding poten- tially relevant information about the objects and the propagation environment. We propose a Bayesian framework for multiobject tracking that relates object states to raw complex-valued signals via a physics-based superpositional model. The model combines a physics-based array manifold, such as radar steering vectors or the replica vectors of matched-field processing, with a latent field. This latent field is a family of context-dependent signal- power distributions that captures the effects of the objects and the propagation environment and is shared across objects and time. It is parameterized by a conditional normalizing flow, which is trained during runtime without labeled data by maximizing an evidence lower bound (ELBO) derived from the Bayesian model. Learning and inference are thus coupled in a sequential framework. We evaluate the method in simulation and in real-world radio and acoustic experiments, with spatial scales ranging from meters to kilometers, and show that it outperforms detection-based methods.

Abstract:
I axiomatize Berk-Nash equilibrium in decision problems with possibly misspecified models. I specify how a rule--which selects a set of action-belief pairs in a problem--ought to compare a correct forecast with an incorrect one, react to the removal of models, and accommodate additional observations that do not distinguish among the models. Title: Two-point concentration for graph classes admitting sparse vertex deletion

Abstract:
For fixed $p\in(0,1)$, we prove that the maximum number of vertices in an induced subgraph of $G(n,p)$ from a given class is concentrated on two consecutive integers, unifying and extending several earlier results. Title: An asymptotic Jensen-Polya criterion for GRH

Abstract:
The Jensen--Pólya criterion expresses the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH) for Dedekind zeta-functions as a real-rootedness condition on their Jensen polynomials. Previous asymptotic results require large shifts, while computations establish real-rootedness in the Riemann case through a finite range of degrees. Here we study the unshifted family as the degree tends to infinity. For every number field $K$, we prove unconditionally that $J_{K,d}(X)$ is nonzero and has at least $d-C_K\sqrt{d\log d}$ distinct negative real zeros for all sufficiently large $d$, where $C_K>0$ depends only on $K$. Therefore, the proportion of real zeros tends to one with error $O_K(\sqrt{\log d/d})$. The main theorems have been autoformalized in Lean~4 by AxiomProver.

Title: Integrable and non-integrable LR geodesic flows on 5-dimensional 2-step nilpotent Lie groups

Abstract:
We investigate sub-Riemannian geodesic flows on 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie groups endowed with left-invariant Riemannian metrics. Up to isomorphism, there are exactly two such groups: the Heisenberg group $H_5$ and the 5-dimensional nilpotent Lie group with a 2-dimensional commutator subgroup. For each group, we study geodesic flows associated with both left-invariant (LL) and right-invariant (LR) distributions, deriving explicit descriptions of the corresponding geodesics and comparing their integrability properties. While the LL systems are known to be Liouville integrable, and even superintegrable, we show that LR systems are Liouville integrable only in two cases: on the Heisenberg group and, for the second group, on a distinguished invariant level set.

Title: Nonthermal coalescence parameter of light nuclei production in pp collisions at LHC energies

Abstract:
We study the light nucleus production in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $13$~TeV reported by the ALICE Collaboration within the color string fragmentation framework. We adopt the Schwinger mechanism with string tension fluctuations as the particle production mechanism describing the $p_T$ spectrum. The approximately thermal behavior observed in the light-nucleus spectra motivates the use of a perturbative series expansion of the $q$-Gaussian string tension fluctuations around $q=1$. The resulting $p_T$ spectrum is expressed as a perturbative series expansion around the thermal distribution with nonthermal corrections given by Gamma distributions, providing closed forms for the effective temperature, moments, and cumulants. In the superstatistical framework, the associated temperature fluctuations show that the medium in which light nuclei are produced is out of equilibrium. Additionally, we derive closed formulas for the coalescence parameter at arbitrary order, which agree well with experimental data. Our results also show that the mass--temperature relation ($T_N/m_N \approx AT_A/m_A$) between the nucleons and nuclei is not preserved in the coalescence process.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Are these ‘GGT-less primes’ already known?
Tags: number-theory, prime-numbers, twin-primes, goldbachs-conjecture

Question:
I was playing around with Goldbach representations and came up with the following class of primes.

Consider an even integer $n$ that can be written as a sum of two odd primes,

$$
n=p+q,\qquad p\le q.
$$

For a fixed $n$, define $GGT(n)$ to be the largest possible value of $q$ among all such pairs $(p,q)$.

Since the case $q=n-3$ is trivial whenever $n-3$ is prime, exclude all such $n$. Let $n'$ denote the remaining even integers.

Call an odd prime $q$ a GGT prime if $q=GGT(n')$ for at least one such $n'$, and a GGT-less prime if this never happens.

Computing the GGT-less primes gives

$$
5,11,17,29,41,59,71,101,107,149,\ldots
$$

This sequence looks very similar to the sequence of smaller members of twin-prime pairs, apart from $3$. In fact, every GGT-less prime is the smaller member of a twin-prime pair.

To see this, let $q$ be a GGT-less prime. Consider $q+5$. The pair

$$
(5,q)
$$

is one Goldbach representation of $q+5$. For $q$ not to be $GGT(q+5)$, there must be another Goldbach representation whose larger prime exceeds $q$. Since the smaller prime must then be less than $5$, the only possible odd prime is $3$. Thus the only possibility is

$$
q+5=3+(q+2).
$$

Therefore $q+2$ must also be prime. Hence $q$ and $q+2$ form a twin-prime pair, and $q$ is its smaller member.

The converse, however, is false. The first counterexample is $137$. Although $137$ and $139$ are twin primes,

$$
148=11+137.
$$

Any Goldbach representation of $148$ with a larger prime than $137$ would have to use an odd prime less than $11$. The only possibilities for the smaller prime are therefore $3,5,7$, giving

$$
3+145,\qquad 5+143,\qquad 7+141,
$$

none of which is a Goldbach representation. Hence

$$
GGT(148)=137,
$$

so $137$ is the smaller member of a twin-prime pair but is not GGT-less.

I searched OEIS for

$$
5,11,17,29,41,59,71,101,107,149
$$

and did not find a matching sequence. A closely related sequence is OEIS A178128: after omitting the initial term $5$, the first nine terms agree, although the two sequences eventually diverge.

Is this class of GGT-less primes already known under another definition? If not, is there any heuristic or known result suggesting whether infinitely many GGT-less primes should exist?

Site: Chemistry Stack Exchange
Title: Why does lithium metal form dendrites easily in batteries?
Tags: electrochemistry, metal

Question:
Rechargeable lithium metal batteries remain an elusive goal because of metal dendrite formation. During charging, lithium ions are attracted to the metal plate and deposited on it. Such an atomic deposition is akin to chemical vapor deposition (CVD), and according to this answer, if the deposition process is reversible, it can help loosely attached atoms to rearrange into more compact forms. Considering that the recharging process is highly reversible, it should have smoothed out any irregularities during recharging.

So why do dendrites form despite the reversible nature of lithium ion deposition? My guess is that in CVD atoms just bump around randomly, whereas in recharging batteries lithium ions are guided by electric fields. Because metals have a much higher electrical conductivity than electrolytes, once a dendrite forms it can greatly shorten the distance and resistance between electrodes, which attracts more lithium ions to deposit on it, creating a positive feedback. However, such an explanation can’t explain why other metals like lead don’t form dendrites.

Title: For purposes of estate planning, how do we define a specialized role for handling personal things of low financial value, such as clothing?
Tags: wills, trusts-and-estates, death, estate-planning

Question:
Suppose that we were to create a living trust, for an end-of-life plan.

How do we define a specialized role for handling property of low financial value, such as clothing and used kitchen-ware?

In layman's terms, the legal papers must establish a job title for the man or woman responsible for disposing of half-way used shampoo bottles, and other cheap items in the home.

In informal parlance, we could have something like this:

"My eldest daughter shall deal with all of my cheaper stuff, unless my daughter passes away before me, in which case, the trustee will deal with all of my cheaper stuff.

Whoever gets the cheap stuff should be well paid to sort through it.

Whoever sorts through my cheap stuff should try to give as much of it to charity as possible, instead of throwing all of it away in the trash"

An Attempt

Definition of Tangible Personal Property

Notwithstanding any other provision, for all purposes of this Trust, 'Tangible Personal Property' shall include clothing, furniture, personal effects, and household goods. Additionally, 'Tangible Personal Property' shall expressly exclude jewelry, precious metals of any kind, paper currency, and shall exclude all financial accounts.

Definition of Tangible Personal Property Manager

Notwithstanding any other provision, for all purposes of this Trust, the 'Tangible Personal Property Manager' shall be tasked with the sorting, and disposing of, the Grantor's tangible personal property.

Distribution to the Tangible Personal Property Manager

The grantor gives all of the grantor’s tangible personal property, as defined herein, to the tangible personal property manager.

The tangible personal property manager shall sort through the grantor's tangible personal property.

The tangible personal property manager shall donate approximately 50%, or more, of the grantor's clothing to a thrift store, and the tangible personal property manager shall dispose of the remaining tangible personal property as they see fit.

The tangible personal property manager, as defined in this amendment, shall be the eldest daughter of the grantor, if the eldest daughter of the grantor survives the grantor.

If the eldest daughter of the grantor does not survive the grantor, the trustee shall be the designated the tangible personal property manager.

Special Compensation Provision

For the specific task of sorting and disposing of tangible personal property under this article, the the tangible personal property manager shall be compensated at an hourly rate (R). R is defined as the numerical product of $400.00 multiplied by the quotient of the United States employment cost index (ECI) for the year prior to the grantor’s death divided by the employment cost index for the first quarter of the year 2026 (as computed by the U.S. Bureau of labor statistics). The tangible personal property manager's billable time for the task of disposing of tangible personal property is strictly capped at a maximum of 40 hours. Additionally, the tangible personal property manager's billable time for this specific task is strictly capped at a maximum of three thousand United States Dollars.

One problem with this poor attempt at putting the my wishes into writing is that the final trust document must be very short, and my writing style fails to be concise. Another problem, is that I am not an attorney, and my writing style is informal, at times.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: When is $f(x,y)=0$ a graph over $x$ when $f(0,0)=f_y(0,0)=0$?
Tags: real-analysis, calculus, multivariable-calculus, implicit-function-theorem

Question:
Some background

Let $f(x,y)$ be a smooth function near $(0,0)$, and $f(0,0)=0$.

By implicit function theorem, if $f_y(0,0)\ne 0$, then $f(x,y)=0$ near $(0,0)$ is a graph over $x$.

However, this is merely a sufficient condition. In fact, $f(x,y):=x-y^3$ has $f_y(0,0)=0$ but $f(x,y)=0$ is the graph of $y=x^{1/3}$ near $(0,0)$.

In general, when $f_y(0,0)=0$, it seems reasonable to look at the Taylor expansion of $f$.

Let $P_k(x,y)$ be the $k$-th order Taylor polynomial of $f(x,y)$, and let $P_{k_0}(x,y)$ be the least order Taylor polynomial such that both $x$ and $y$ are present (a variable can be absent because of the corresponding coefficients being zero.)

We assume such $k_0$ exists.

Question:

Is is true that, near $(0,0)$, $f(x,y)=0$ is a graph over $x$ if and only if $P_{k_0}(x,y)=0$ is a graph over $x$?

This seems to be closely related to the Malgrange preparation theorem, which states that

If $f(0,0)=\partial_y f(0,0)=\cdots=\partial_y^{n-1} f(0,0)=0$ while $\partial_y^{n} f(0,0)\ne 0$, then
$$f(x,y)=c(x,y)(y^{n}+a_{n-1}(x)y^{n-1}+\cdots+a_1(x)y+a_0(x))$$
where $c$ and $a_i$'s are smooth and $c(0,0)\ne 0$.

N.B. The polynomial part is not necessarily of the same order as the $P_{k_0}$ defined above.

In fact, using the theorem above, one can show that if $f_{yy}(0,0)\ne 0$ and $f_x(0,0)\ne 0$, then $\{f=0\}$ cannot be a graph near $0$:

$$f=0 \qquad \Leftrightarrow \qquad y^2+a_1(x)y+a_0(x)=0$$

which means

$$y=\frac{-a_1(x)\pm\sqrt{a_1(x)^2-4a_0(x)}}{2}$$

Note that the discriminant $\Delta(x):=a_1(x)^2-4a_0(x)$ satisfies $\Delta(0)=0$ and $\Delta'(0)=-4a_0'(0)=\frac{-4 f_x(0,0)}{c(0,0)}\ne 0$. Thus, $\{f=0\}$ near $(0,0)$ lies either in $\{x\ge 0\}$ or $\{x\le 0\}$ and each value of $x$ corresponds to two values of $y$ (so it is not a graph over $x$).

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Li-Campeau syndrome (LICAS)

Draft text:
----

Li–Campeau syndrome (LICAS) is a rare autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder caused by pathogenic variants in both copies of the UBR7 gene. Reported features include developmental delay, intellectual disability, distinctive facial features, hypothyroidism, and variable heart and genital abnormalities. [ref: Li-Campeau syndrome (Concept ID: C5543068), MedGen] [ref: Eighth case of Li-Campeau syndrome in a Turkish patient caused by a novel pathogenic variant in UBR7 and expanding the phenotype, American Journal of Medical Genetics Part A]

== Signs and symptoms ==
In the original series, seven children from six unrelated families were evaluated between the ages of two and ten years. All had global developmental delay and intellectual disability. Low muscle tone was common, and some children had no speech. Six had seizures beginning in infancy or early childhood. [ref: Li-Campeau syndrome; LICAS, Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man]

Other findings in that series included cardiac abnormalities in five children, hypothyroidism in four, and short stature in five. All six boys had genital abnormalities, predominantly undescended testes; one also had a small penis. Two siblings had microcephaly. These counts describe the original cohort.

Reported facial features include drooping upper eyelids, widely spaced eyes, a prominent forehead, thick eyebrows, low-set ears, and a long philtrum. Strabismus, epicanthal folds, downward-slanting eyelid openings, and a high-arched palate have also been described. Less common findings include scoliosis, increased body hair, underdeveloped kneecaps, long fingers, a single transverse palmar crease, and gastrointestinal dysmotility.

Cardiac findings have included atrial and ventricular septal defects, patent ductus arteriosus, and patent foramen ovale. Brain imaging was performed in four children in the initial cohort. Reported abnormalities included enlarged ventricles, cortical atrophy, a thin corpus callosum, delayed myelination, and nonspecific white matter changes.

== Genetics ==
The condition is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous pathogenic variants in UBR7, located on chromosome 14q32.12. The variants identified in the original families segregated with the disorder in a pattern consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

Reported variants included frameshift, nonsense, splice-site, and missense variants, as well as an intragenic deletion. The investigators predicted a loss-of-function mechanism. Although variant-specific functional studies were not performed, cells obtained from three patients showed loss of UBR7 protein.

In an independent case reported in 2023, an affected child had a homozygous splice-site variant, while each parent carried one copy. The investigators predicted that the variant would impair UBR7 function.

== Diagnosis ==
In the original cohort, the genetic findings were identified through exome or genome sequencing. In the 2023 case report, exome sequencing identified the UBR7 variant, and Sanger sequencing confirmed its presence in the child and carrier status in the parents.

== History ==
Li and colleagues described seven affected individuals with biallelic UBR7 variants in a study published online in December 2020 and in the January 2021 issue of the American Journal of Human Genetics. [ref: UBR7 functions with UBR5 in the Notch signaling pathway and is involved in a neurodevelopmental syndrome with epilepsy, ptosis, and hypothyroidism, American Journal of Human Genetics] An additional case was reported by Edizadeh and colleagues in 2023.
==Research==
Experiments involving the Caenorhabditis elegans counterpart of UBR7 identified developmental defects and altered Notch signaling in germline stem cells, suggesting a role for the protein in developmental signaling.

In 2023, researchers generated an induced pluripotent stem cell line from blood cells of a seven-year-old boy with the syndrome. The patient carried two different UBR7 variants. [ref: Establishment of a novel human induced pluripotent stem cell line (SIPDi001-A) with compound heterozygous mutations in the UBR7 gene from a Li-Campeau syndrome patient, Stem Cell Research]

== References ==

== External links ==

* [https://www.omim.org/entry/619189 Li–Campeau syndrome] in Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM 619189)

Title: Generalized Transition Fronts and Spectral Speed Asymptotics in Heterogeneous Cooperative Systems

Abstract:
We study generalized transition fronts for cooperative reaction--diffusion systems with spatially periodic and time-dependent coefficients. We obtain sufficient conditions for the existence of fronts and necessary constraints on their propagation speeds in terms of generalized principal eigenvalues. In the almost-periodic case, we identify the two spectral thresholds and examine the attainment of the critical speed under additional hypotheses on the normalized linear evolution. We then investigate the large-advection limit and construct a time-periodic example showing that a stationary spectral characterization need not extend to time-dependent flows. For symmetric cooperative systems in stationary periodic shears with equal diffusion matrices, we obtain explicit correction terms for the minimal speed in both the small- and large-diffusion limits. The two expansions follow from periodic eigenvalue perturbation, localization near a maximal streamline, and minimization over the exponential weight. We also establish a higher-order large-advection expansion and present numerical illustrations independent of the analytic proofs.

Title: Grammar Control for Language Learning with Sequential Monte Carlo and Small Language Models

Abstract:
Second language learners benefit from exposure to level-appropriate grammar in interactive language use. While prompted frontier language models can usually produce target grammar structures, less resource-intensive models that can be run on device often fail in this task. We use sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to steer dialogue turn generation in small lan- language models toward target grammar constructions from an expert-developed pedagogical resource. With a minimal set of hand-coded potential functions, SMC achieves near-perfect coverage of target grammar, enabling small models to outperform state-of-the-art results from models 140 times larger. We also use code synthesis with frontier models to generate new potentials, showing that our method scales to hundreds of target grammar skills with no need for additional training or supervised data.

Site: Physics Stack Exchange
Title: What if you lost the gravitational attraction holding you to Earth?
Tags: newtonian-mechanics, newtonian-gravity, centrifugal-force

Question:
This is a question I began to consider recently. From my knowledge of high school physics, I knew you'd be moving along your initial tangential path with a constant velocity (approximately), which would depend on your latitude. So for the sake of the question, I went with specifying that you're at the equator, and all external forces are negligible (air resistance, buoyancy force, outside gravity, etc).

"What if" isn't very precise, though, so I guess a more accurate question would be to ask about your experience in a non-inertial frame, as well as how long it'd take you to reach the Karman Line (100 km). From a reddit search, I found a similar question with an approach that treated your Y separation distance from earth as increasing linearly with acceleration.

They approximated this acceleration by taking

$a_{c}=r\omega^{2}$

$a_{c}=(6.37\cdot 10^{6})(\frac{2\pi}{86400})^{2}\cong 0.0337 $ m/s

Then, using the uniformly accelerated motion equations,

$\frac{2\Delta y}{a_{c}}=t^{2}$

$\sqrt{\frac{2\cdot 100000}{0.0337}}=t\cong 40$ minutes

This method didn't really sit right with me (the acceleration is inward, so how would it affect separation distance? After all, in centripetal motion, speed is constant), so I took it upon myself to find an alternative method. I started by drawing the earth as a circle, and assuming I was a point on top of that circle. Since there would be no gravitational influence on me, my velocity would remain in the +x direction, tangential to the circle. Point "A" is my original location on top of the earth, point "B" is the earth's center, and point "C" is my location after a +x displacement in a certain time period. AC is perpendicular to BA, so a right angle is created, and a hypotenuse can be drawn as BC.

BA will always be equal to the radius of the earth.
AC, as stated previously, is the +x displacement, which I'll denote as x.
That leaves BC, which is the distance between the center of the earth and my new location.

Let's go back to the definition of the Karmen line. It's 100km from any point on the surface, which means BC is equal to the radius of the earth + the Karmen line.

Using the Pythagorean Theorem,

$BA^{2}+AC^{2}=BC^{2}$

$(x)^2+(R_{e})^2=(R_{e}+K)^2$

$(x)^2+(6.37\cdot 10^6)^2=(6.37\cdot 10^6+100000)^2$

$x\cong 1133137$ meters

V, the tangential velocity, can be calculated,

$v=r\omega=(6.37\cdot 10^6)(\frac{2\pi}{86400})\cong 463$ m/s

Now, with the uniform motion equations,

$t=\frac{x}{v}$

$t=\frac{1133137}{463}\cong 40$ minutes

Now, I must say, this was a really exciting result. It's nearly identical to the time duration calculated with the previous method. If you generalize the distance for both equations and graph them, you'll see that the difference between their calculations is very minuscule until about 5-6 orders of magnitude (of distance).

What I'd like to know is

Is either result accurate? If so, why does the acceleration approximation work for shorter distances? If not, what's the correct approach?

What if drag comes into play? I share the same speed as the atmosphere w.r.t earth, so does it affect the results at all?

Title: Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation

Abstract:
We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

Title: AFDM-ISAC Design Amalgamating FMCW Radar and Carrier Aggregation

Abstract:
Carrier-aggregation (CA)-assisted affine frequency division multiplexing (AFDM) is conceived for integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. A frequency-modulated continuous-wave (FMCW)-inspired dechirping receiver is developed to exploit the inherent pulse-compression property of AFDM chirp subcarriers for accurate delay-Doppler estimation. To further enhance sensing performance, a pair of CA schemes is proposed. The Type-I CA scheme improves sensing accuracy by aggregating echo signals across multiple CA bands prior to radar processing, thereby reducing estimation error with low hardware overhead. The Type-II CA scheme enhances range resolution by effectively enlarging the sensing bandwidth, where chirps from different CA bands are designed to form a continuous set of chirp signals. Based on this principle, variable subcarrier sensing and asynchronous sensing schemes are developed. For the communication receiver, the generalized input-output relationship of AFDM is derived under both fractional delay and fractional Doppler (FDFD) channels. To address the challenge of FDFD estimation, a cross-domain sensing-assisted channel estimation (CDS-CE) scheme is proposed to facilitate time-domain delay-Doppler parameter estimation and affine-domain channel coefficient recovery. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves significant improvements in sensing accuracy and resolution, as well as in channel estimation performance compared with state-of-the-art methods.

Bloxd.io is a free online video game, released in January of 2021 by an independent developer, Arthur Benedict Baker. It is a sandbox game inspired by the games Minecraft, and Roblox. Bloxd.io has many gamemodes to choose from. The gamemodes range from being Open world, games such as survival, creative, and Bloxdsmp where you can gather resources, farm, and build houses. Another genre of gamemodes is PvP. PvP gamemodes include bedwars, Skyblock, and cube warfare. In these gamemodes, it is fast paced, and player will need to utilize their material to the max. Skill games are another type of gamemode mostly including parkour, where you would have to jump over obstacles to make it to the end. Bloxd.io also has a feature where you can create a new world where you have the power of using commands and code blocks to make your own mini games. None of the gamemodes contain a pay-wall [ref: Bloxd.io Wiki, bloxd-io.fandom.com]

Bloxd.io has only 1 rank, Super Rank. Super Rank Is a 30 days paid rank added on December 18, 2024. The rank is not pay-to-win because it doesn't give the user any gameplay advantage. The rank's perks are cosmetics. Spending $10 on Super Rank would give you the following, visual badges, name colors (would allow you to change the color of your username), capes, and remove all advertisements. Title: Resonant Amplification of Demographic Noise in Stochastic Common-Pool Resource Dynamics

Abstract:
Common-pool resources are vulnerable to overexploitation, yet many social-ecological systems exhibit persistent oscillations. We introduce a stochastic eco-evolutionary model in which harvesting strategies and resource availability shape one another. In the infinite population limit the system approaches a stable state through damped oscillations. Demographic noise continually excites these modes, generating instead robust macroscopic quasi-cycles, whose frequencies depend on the noise ratio, the relative timescale between strategy and resource, and the harvesting pressure. The model reproduces the distinct frequency peaks, observed in empirical global fish-landings data for high- and low-income countries, showing that persistent environmental fluctuations can emerge naturally from demographic noise.

Title: Dice enterprises and polynomial approximation: uniform query tails

Abstract:
A binary-output dice enterprise uses independent rolls of a die with unknown face probabilities $\mathbf p$ (along with fair coin flips) to simulate a coin with bias $f(\mathbf p)$. We determine which power-law tails, uniform over the closed probability simplex, are attainable for the number $N$ of rolls. For continuous $f$ with values in $(0,1)$ and $q>0$, some enterprise for $f$ satisfies $\sup_{\mathbf p}\mathbb{P}_{\mathbf p}(N>n)=O(n^{-q})$ if and only if $f$ can be approximated uniformly by polynomials of degree $k$ with error $O(k^{-2q})$. When this holds, the same tail bound is attained by an oblivious enterprise, which chooses its number of rolls before rolling. The characterization extends to multiple dice, with total degree on a product of simplices; it then suffices to roll the dice in a fixed cyclic order. For $q>1$, these enterprises have a uniformly bounded expected number of rolls.

Title: The assembly of dusty galaxies at $z \geq 4$: grain growth and the evolutionary origin of the dust-to-stellar-mass scatter

Abstract:
Understanding dust evolution is essential for interpreting the properties of galaxies across cosmic time. Nearby galaxies have revealed a detailed picture of dust enrichment, but whether the same picture applies in the early Universe remains unclear. Here we explore the origin of interstellar dust in simulated galaxies at $z \sim 5$. Starting from the dust-to-stellar mass relation, we select five simulated star-forming galaxies with $SFR> 1 M_\odot yr^{-1}$ and $ log(M_\star/M_\odot) > 8$. We focus on three low-mass systems with comparable stellar masses ($log(M_\star/M_\odot) \sim 8.7$) but significantly different dust masses ($log(M_{\rm dust}/M_\odot) \sim 5.1-6.2$), to investigate the origin of the scatter in the relation. Our analysis combines outputs from the cosmological hydrodynamical simulation dustyGadget, a semi-analytical model for stellar dust production, and radiative-transfer post-processing with SKIRT. We confirm that stellar dust production alone reproduces only the low-dust branch of the relation. Grain growth is required to recover both its S-shape and the observed scatter, as established for nearby galaxies. The transition to efficient grain growth occurs at lower metallicity than locally, consistent with the denser interstellar medium of high-redshift systems. Differences in dust content reflect different stages of galaxy assembly. Progressively longer star formation histories lead to greater chemical enrichment and denser ISM, promoting increasingly efficient grain growth. We therefore identify the assembly stage as the key regulator of dust growth at high redshift. Mock observations show that JWST multi-band imaging can reveal the structural diversity of galaxies within the scatter, although the reconstruction of clumpy morphologies may remain incomplete. Their dust continuum emission remains below the sensitivity of current ALMA continuum surveys.

Title: First-principles calculations of far-wing absorption in He-broadened CO2 infrared spectra

Abstract:
We report theoretical predictions and modeling of the far-wing absorption of CO2 broadened by He over a wide temperature range (200-1000 K), which are relevant for exoplanet atmosphere studies. Accurate modeling of He-broadened CO2 absorption is essential for opacity calculations used to characterize the composition, structure, and climate of exoplanet atmospheres. In particular, the strong CO2 band at 4.3 mum has been clearly identified in the spectra of several exoplanets observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations were first performed to predict absorption in the far wings of the 4.3 mum band of CO2. The resulting predictions show excellent agreement with available experimental data at room temperature. The theoretical predictions and measured data were then used to parameterize an impact energy-corrected sudden model, which allowed us to accurately reproduce the far-wing absorption of He-broadened CO2 in several infrared spectral regions over the (200-1000) K temperature range. Finally, for applications to exoplanet atmosphere opacity calculations, we derived temperature-dependent chi-factor corrections that account for the sub-Lorentzian behavior of the far wing of the major infrared bands of CO2.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Axiomatizability of the class of relations whose relation classes form a partition.
Tags: model-theory, relations

Question:
We all know what equivalence classes are, but less well-known are their generalization, called relation classes. Given a binary relation $R$ on a set $S$, and an element $a \in S$, the relation class associated with $a$ is the set $\{x \in S | aRx\}$. This is clearly a generalization of the definition of equivalence classes.

It is very well-known that if $R$ is an equivalence relation on a set $S$, then the set of relation classes of $R$ is a partition of $S$. But what most people don't know is that the converse is actually false. For a counterexample, consider the relation $R$ on the integers $\mathbb{Z}$ defined as follow: $xRy \iff y = x+1$. That relation is neither reflexive, symmetric, nor transitive, but the set of its relation classes is the set of all singletons in $\mathbb{Z}$, and hence is a partition of $\mathbb{Z}$.

My question is this. Let $C$ be the class of binary relations $R$ such that the set of its relation classes is a partition of the underlying set $S$ of $R$. Is $C$ a first-order axiomatizable class? If so, is it finitely axiomatizable? Also, bonus question, if $C$ is not itself axiomatizable, is its theory $Th(C)$ finitely axiomatizable?

Answer A:
Unless I'm missing something, seems it's finitely axiomatizable...

Write $x\in R_a$ to mean $aR x.$

Then we just want to say $\forall x\exists a\; x\in R_a$ and $\forall x,a,b, \;x \in R_a\cap R_b \to R_a = R_b,$ which are expressible as sentences, e.g.  $R_a= R_b$ is expressible as $\forall z \; aRz \leftrightarrow b R z.$

Answer B:
Yes, you can just write down that the set of relation classes form a partition, more or less directly from the definitions.

Here are the axioms:

$\forall x\exists y\, xRy$

$\forall y\exists x\, xRy$

$\forall x\forall x'\forall y\,(xRy\land x'Ry\rightarrow \forall z\,(xRz\leftrightarrow x'Rz))$

Writing $[x]=\{y\in S\mid xRy\}$ for the relation class of $x$, 1 says that every relation class $[x]$ is non-empty, 2 says that every element $y$ is in some relation class $[x]$ (so the union of the relation classes is all of $S$), and 3 says that the relation classes are pairwise disjoint. Explicitly, it says that if $y$ is in both $[x]$ and $[x']$, then $[x]=[x']$.

You might be interested to note that if $R$ has the property that $[x]=[x']$ implies $x=x'$ (i.e., distinct elements have distinct relation classes), then the relation classes partition $S$ if and only if $R^{-1}$ is a surjective function $S\to S$. This is the case for your example, where the function is $y\mapsto y-1$.

In general, we have that the relation classes partition $S$ if and only if $R^{-1}$ is a surjective function $S\to S/{\sim}$, where $\sim$ is the equivalence relation $x\sim y \iff [x]=[y]$.

Draft text:
Haitham bin Shunayf bin Raddad Al-Jadaani (; 1979 – 22 April 2011) was a Saudi Quran reciter, imam, and khatib from Jeddah. He was known for his murattal recitation in the Hafs 'an Asim narration and for holding ijazahs in a number of Quranic readings. [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] [ref: الترجمة الشخصية للشيخ هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, ar.islamway.net]

== Biography ==
Al-Jadaani was born in Jeddah on 8 Rajab 1399 AH (1979). He completed his primary, intermediate, and secondary education in the city, then studied at the Qassim branch of Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University, graduating from it. [ref: القارئ الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني رحمه الله, haithamaljadani.com] He married twice and had five children.

== Education and ijazahs ==
He began memorising the Quran in the Quranic study circles of Jeddah as a child under Sheikh Muhammad Bafil and a group of students of knowledge, until he was granted an ijazah in it. He then travelled to the Qassim region in pursuit of knowledge, where he attended the lessons of Sheikh Muhammad ibn Salih al-Uthaymeen, and after al-Uthaymeen's death he continued studying with his students.

He travelled outside Saudi Arabia to receive the Quran from those proficient in its narrations, obtaining ijazahs in several readings, including Hafs 'an Asim, Shu'bah 'an Asim, Al-Bazzi and Qunbul from Ibn Kathir, and Qalun from Nafi'.

== Career ==
He served as imam and khatib of Noor Al-Rahman Mosque in the Al-Salamah district of Jeddah until his death. He was already listed among the well-known reciters of Jeddah several years before his death. [ref: المساجد التي سيؤم بها قراء العالم الإسلامي هذا العام, mazameer.com]

== Recitations ==
Al-Jadaani recorded the complete murattal Quran in the Hafs 'an Asim narration, and also recorded recitations in the Al-Bazzi 'an Ibn Kathir narration as well as recordings of the tarawih and tahajjud prayers. [ref: مصاحف هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني, midad.com] His recitations remain available on a number of Quran audio platforms and download archives. [ref: تلاوات القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, audio.islamweb.net] [ref: هيثم بن شنيف الجدعاني: تلاوات القرآن الكريم بصوته, ar.assabile.com] [ref: القارئ هيثم الجدعاني, tahaquran.com]

== Death ==
On Friday 22 April 2011, Al-Jadaani drowned in the sea near the shore of Dhahban, north of Jeddah, during a family outing on a boat. When his nine-year-old nephew Abdulaziz fell from the boat, his father Abdulrahim and his uncle Haitham entered the water to rescue him; the boat's captain succeeded in saving the child, but the two brothers drowned. [ref: وفاة الشيخ هيثم الجدعاني إمام وخطيب جامع نور الرحمن بجدة, dd-sunnah.net]

The funeral prayer was offered for the two brothers after the Fajr prayer on Saturday 23 April 2011 at Al-Thunayan Mosque in Jeddah, and they were buried in the Dhahban cemetery.

== Legacy ==
After his death, Saudi Arabia's Quran Radio broadcast selections of his recitations, and his recordings continued to circulate among listeners. Several Quran audio platforms have kept his complete murattal recitation available for streaming and download.

Title: An Adaptive Transferable Neural Network for Partial Differential Equations with Anisotropic or Sharp Solutions

Abstract:
Transferable neural network (TransNet) has demonstrated great potential for solving partial differential equations (PDEs) with high accuracy and efficiency. However, it struggles significantly when dealing with PDEs featuring anisotropy or sharp solutions. In this work, we propose an adaptive transferable neural network (A-TransNet), a novel machine learning framework that adaptively expands neurons in regions with large solution gradients to effectively capture complex solution behaviors. Instead of relying on training or random sampling, the location parameters of newly added neurons are determined by integrating the active subspaces method and local gradient analysis based on posterior gradient information. This adaptive strategy enables neurons to be allocated where they are most needed, thereby improving the resolution of anisotropic and sharp features without additional computational costs. Moreover, the shape parameters of new neurons are automatically determined from the neuron density induced by their locations, further enhancing the network representation capability. An iterative neuron expansion strategy is developed, together with rigorous analysis of stability, a posteriori error estimation, and convergence of the proposed A-TransNet method. Extensive numerical experiments on challenging PDE problems with anisotropic and sharp solutions demonstrate that A-TransNet achieves superior accuracy, efficiency, and robustness compared with existing methods.

Site: Stats Stack Exchange
Title: Constraints on cross-variograms and correlation range under second-order stationarity
Tags: stationarity, spatial, cross-correlation, geostatistics

Question:
Consider residuals from two models evaluated at times $t_i$ and $t_j$.
Let $e_i(s)$ and $e_j(s)$ be second-order stationary residual fields.

Define the cross-covariance, cross-variogram, and cross-correlation as

$$
C_{ij}(h) = \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(e_i(s), e_j(s+h)\right),
$$

$$
\gamma_{ij}(h) = \text{cross-variogram},
$$

$$
\rho_{ij}(h) = \frac{C_{ij}(h)}{\sqrt{C_{ii}(0)\,C_{jj}(0)}} .
$$

From the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality, the cross-covariance is bounded by

$$
C_{ii}(0)\,C_{jj}(0) \ge \left| C_{ij}(h) \right|^2 .
$$

Similarly, the cross-variogram satisfies

$$
\gamma_{ii}(h)\,\gamma_{jj}(h) \ge \left| \gamma_{ij}(h) \right|^2 .
$$

Under second-order stationarity, the relationship between the cross-variogram
and cross-covariance is

$$
\gamma_{ij}(h)
= C_{ij}(0)
- \frac{1}{2}\left[ C_{ij}(h) + C_{ij}(-h) \right].
$$

The pseudo cross-variogram can be written as

$$
\tilde{\gamma}_{ij}(h)
= \frac{1}{2}\left[ C_{ii}(0) + C_{jj}(0) \right] - C_{ij}(h).
$$

From these inequalities, and in particular from Cauchy--Schwarz, it follows
that any structured component present in the cross-variogram must also be
present in both marginal variograms (though the converse is not required).

Now assume that the residuals at $t_i$ and $t_j$ are each modeled using a
nugget + spherical variogram, and that both marginal variograms have
approximately the same correlation range (say $\approx 20\ \text{km}$).

My questions are:

Do the above constraints imply that, if the cross-variogram exhibits a
structured component, its range must be of the same order as the marginal
ranges (i.e., close to $20$ km), while differences may mainly appear in the
nugget-to-sill ratio or overall magnitude?

If one is interested in a mean spatial correlation between the two residual
fields, is it correct that

$$
\left| \int_A \rho_{ij}(h)\,dh \right|
\le
\min\!\left(
\int_A \rho_{ii}(h)\,dh,\;
\int_A \rho_{jj}(h)\,dh
\right),
$$

i.e. that the integrated cross-correlation over an area is bounded by the
corresponding marginal integrals?

In contrast, if the relationship between the snapshot residuals is intrinsic
(so that $\rho_{ij}(h)$ is scale-independent), does a mean areal correlation
remain well defined, or is it fundamentally undefined in that case?

I would appreciate confirmation or correction of this interpretation,
particularly regarding the implications for cross-variogram range and
spatially averaged correlation.

Title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras

Abstract:
We classify the connected components of support $τ$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $τ$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $τ$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $τ$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $τ$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.

Site: Biology Stack Exchange
Title: Does hyperphosphorylated tau reactivate latent HSV1 infections in Alzheimer’s?
Tags: virology

Question:
Researchers have shown that HSV1 mediates the tau phosphorylation signatures that characterize LOAD (late-onset Alzheimer's disease), but I haven't read a compelling explanation for why HSV1 would want to do this. Although not explicitly stated, I am curious whether several papers, when viewed together, indicate that hyperphosphorylated tau reactivates latent HSV1 infections in LOAD.

Cuddy et al. (2020) showed that neuronal hyperexcitability and DLK-JNK signaling can reactivate latent HSV1 infections. Separately, researchers have shown:

HSV1 (directly through viral kinases, as well as indirectly) creates the tau phosphorylation patterns that characterize LOAD (Wozniak et al., 2009);

hyperphosphorylated tau with HSV1-mediated tau phosphorylation signatures are preferentially released into the extracellular space (Sindi et al., 2024);

neuronal hyperexcitability is induced by (apparently extracellular) tau with HSV1-phosphorylation signatures (Brown et al., 2023); and,

the DLK-JNK signaling pathway is activated by LOAD-characteristic phosphorylated tau (Li et al., 2024).

Essentially, HSV1-hyperphosphorylated tau appears to induce neuronal hyperexcitability and signal through DLK-JNK. According to Cuddy et al. (2020), this should reactivate latent HSV1 infections.

Tau's unique phosphorylation signatures in LOAD are essential to these steps. My impression is that tau's unique phosphorylation signatures are necessary for its signaling through DLK-JNK, and also for its release into the extracellular space. I imagine the phosphorylation signatures are also essential to tau causing neuronal hyperexcitability, but detailed work about this question is lacking.

According to this hypothesis, HSV1 phosphorylates tau in such an unusual and hard-to-understand way, at least partly because HSV1-hyperphosphorylated tau acts as a key for two locks. For one factor to both induce neuronal hyperexcitability and signal through DLK-JNK, it would likely need to be complex. Sophisticated viruses, such as HSV1, frequently generate complex and mysterious factors that serve multiple purposes.

As far as I know, the above are novel observations. If shown conclusively, they would be a compelling explanation connecting HSV1 to the form and function of hyperphosphorylated tau in LOAD. In particular, they would at least partly explain tau's peculiar phosphorylation signatures and why hyperphosphorylated tau appears in LOAD. The signatures enable tau to be secreted from cells, signal through DLK-JNK, and cause neuronal hyperexcitability. According to this hypothesis, the reason hyperphosphorylated tau appears in LOAD is that it reactivates latent HSV1 infections (probably among other reasons).

Does hyperphosphorylated tau reactivate latent HSV1 infections in LOAD?

References:

Brown, J., Camporesi, E., Lantero-Rodriguez, J. et al. Tau in cerebrospinal fluid induces neuronal hyperexcitability and alters hippocampal theta oscillations. acta neuropathol commun 11, 67 (2023). https://doi.org/10.1186/s40478-023-01562-5

This paper appears to suggest that in AD patients around the middle of disease progression, tau phosphorylated at threonine 181 causes neuronal hyperactivity. Other papers have shown that HSV1 infection causes phosphorylation at T181 but have not articulated whether it does so with a viral kinase or by manipulating host kinases. T181 is a phosphorylation signature that is present in all stages of LOAD.

The tau used in the paper's experiments was approximately the average phenotype of tau drawn from the average AD patient. Two important points: 1) any AD patient with Aβ42, Aβ40, total tau (t-tau) and tau phosphorylated at T181 was eligible for their tau to participate in this study (patients' CSF was where the tau was sourced from); 2) the tau of all patients was pooled together. The paper doesn't say how many AD patients donated CSF. In order to have enough tau for these experiments, I assume the researchers must have needed upwards of two dozen AD patients. Given this sample size, I assume all stages of AD were represented adequately.

Cuddy S, Schinlever AR, Dochnal S, Suzich J, Kundu P, Downs TK, Farah M, Desai B, Boutell C, Cliffe AR. Neuronal hyperexcitability is a DLK-dependent trigger of HSV-1 reactivation that can be induced by IL-1. eLife 2020 Dec 22;9:e58037. doi: 10.7554/eLife.58037. PMID: 33350386

Li S, Roy ER, Wang Y, Watkins T, Cao W. DLK-MAPK Signaling Coupled with DNA Damage Promotes Intrinsic Neurotoxicity Associated with Non-Mutated Tau. Mol Neurobiol. 2024 May;61(5):2978-2995. doi: 10.1007/s12035-023-03720-1. Epub 2023 Nov 13. PMID: 37955806; PMCID: PMC11043018.

This article on the whole focuses on how hyperphosphorylated tau signals through DLK-MAPK generally, but says in the abstract "inhibitors of dual leucine zipper kinase (DLK) and c-Jun N-terminal kinase (JNK) were effective in alleviating wild-type human tau-induced neurodegeneration," indicating that hyperphosphorylated tau signals through DLK-JNK specifically.

Sindi, Ghadir & Ismael, Sazan & Uddin, Reaz & Slepchenko, Kira & Colvin, Robert & Lee, Daewoo. (2024). Endogenous tau released from human ReNCell VM cultures by neuronal activity is phosphorylated at multiple sites. bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology. 10.1101/2024.06.02.597022.

Site: Law Stack Exchange
Title: Is it discriminatory to require documentation for menstrual disorders?
Tags: united-states, discrimination, disabilities, americans-with-disabilities-act

Question:
In some parts of the world, in universities every class absence requires proper documentation to be excused. Suppose a university operated under the following regulations.

If students were unable to attend class due to illnesses, their absences can be excused under the following procedures.

The student registers with the Accommodations officer beforehand and receives treatment for the sickness described in the accommodation letter.

For non-recurring disabilities, students can provide a doctor's note up to 10 days after the final day of continuous treatment.

Menstrual disorders do not require documentation for up to 7 days per calendar month.

After a comprehensive review of all excuses granted last year, the university found that more than half of all excuses including non-medical ones were tied to menstrual disorders. Also, such absences were disproportionately used on Fridays, Mondays, and before and after major holiday seasons, leading faculty to assume that the system was being abused.

The university decided to remove the third article from their regulations, enforcing the blanket documentation requirement for all conditions. Is this a Title IX/ADA/Unruh violation if done in a U.S. university?

Answer A:
Probably no

australia

While discrimination based on sex, gender, pregnancy, and family status is forbidden by Commonwealth and state and territory legislation, there is no specific protection for menstruation and associated effects.

Courts have so far been unwilling to stretch sex or gender discrimination laws to cover it and it is the subject of a current Commonwealth parliamentary inquiry.

Answer B:
No, but...

switzerland

I'm not aware of any special laws concerning Universities, so I believe this is very similar to an "ordinary" work contract, given that the students are usually of age.

Common regulations

While the law is pretty open on details about handling sick employees (just stating that he has still to be paid for a certain time), most work contracts contain clauses handling scenarios similar to the ones stated in the OP. A common regulation is that the employee has to provide a medical report for absences longer than three days. Thus he does not need to go to the doctor for a common flu or similar sickness [other than being expensive, this would simply overload most doctors during the flu season]. The employer can always request a medical report if the absences keep reoccurring and/or they seem dubious.

Now, for personality rights and data protection reasons, a medical report, even if one is mandated and obtained, does usually not include information about why the patient is being treated, just that and what implications it has for the job.

So the doctor would not write

Mr A is my patient and he's having [list of diagnoses] and thus can't work for a week.

but instead

Mr A is under my treatment for illness/an injury and he is unable to work for [number of days].

Menstrual disorders

The provided rule in the OP seems very liberal, with an allowance of 7 days per month. Wikipedia states that there are countries that allow women to take absences during their cycle, but at most up to three days. Even then, it usually requires a medical report that states that that particular woman is suffering from such disorders. A doctor can of course issue a medical report stating the reoccurrence of the condition one is being treated for. The doctor can also be asked to provide a medical report about past events (if possible), if the employer requests one from somebody.

Title: Half-Optimal Induced Matchings in Random Graphs: Online and Low-Degree Algorithms

Abstract:
For many optimization problems on random graphs, most prominently the largest independent set problem, natural algorithms reach only half the optimum, and such factor-two gaps are known to be sharp within broad algorithmic classes. We prove such a gap for finding large induced matchings in Erdős-Rényi random graphs. In the worst case, requiring a matching to be induced turns a polynomial-time solvable problem into an NP-hard one; our results reveal an average-case counterpart. In $G(n,p)$ with $C/n\le p\le 1-κ$, the largest induced matching has size $(1+o(1))L$ with high probability, where $L=\log_{1/(1-p)}(np)$. A simple online greedy algorithm finds an induced matching of size $(1/2-ε)L$, while no online algorithm, even with adaptive inspection order and unbounded computation, finds one of size $(1/2+ε)L$ except with probability $\exp(-Ω(L\log(np)))$. In the sparse regime $p=d/n$, low-degree polynomial algorithms exhibit the same sharp threshold. Our guarantees rest on a maximality principle: with high probability, every maximal induced matching is half-optimal. Greedy outputs a maximal induced matching and our low-degree algorithm a near-maximal one. We bypass the delicate coupling arguments classically used to analyze greedy since Karp. For low-degree hardness, we adapt Wein's overlap gap argument, with forbidden structures that track overlaps between endpoint sets rather than edge sets, since a new edge may join two previously used endpoints and thus encounter no fresh randomness. For online hardness, we give a new and significantly simpler argument that avoids the correlated instances of prior OGP-based proofs: at a suitable stopping time, all pairs involving uninspected vertices remain unrevealed, so a direct first-moment bound suffices.

Let $C$ be the class of nonempty finite linear orders. Of course, $C$ itself is not first-order axiomatizable, not even by an infinite set of sentences. However, it does give rise to a first-order theory $Th(C)$. Is there a finite axiomatization of that theory? There exists a maximum element

There exists a minimum element

Every element other than the maximum has an immediate successor

Every element other than the minimum has an immediate predecessor

Is that really all that is needed, or do you need more? Is there even a finite axiomatization?

Title: Constructions of Variable Modified Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel Gases from Geometrothermodynamics

Abstract:
Understanding the physical origin of the Universe's late-time accelerated expansion remains one of the central open problems in modern cosmology. Geometrothermodynamics (GTD) offers a compelling route to this problem, providing a geometric framework that unifies thermodynamics with contact and Riemannian geometry to encode the equilibrium properties of a physical system directly into its underlying geometric structure. In this work, we employ the GTD formalism to investigate cosmological models capable of explaining the observed accelerated expansion of the Universe. As an important outcome, our simple model exhibits dynamical behavior that provides a reasonable description of the late-time evolution of the Universe. We study the Chaplygin-Jacobi and Chaplygin-Abel gas models and their variable forms within geometrothermodynamics by deriving their thermodynamic relations, entropy, and equations of state. The free parameters of the models are constrained through a Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) analysis using several observational datasets, including cosmic chronometers combined with baryon acoustic oscillations (CC+BAO), DESI DR2 BAO data, DESI DR2 combined with the DES-SN5YR and Union3 Type Ia supernova compilations. The statistical performance of the models is assessed using the Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria (AIC and BIC). We further examine their cosmological evolution through the deceleration parameter, the dark-energy equation-of-state parameter, and higher-order kinematic diagnostics, including the jerk and snap parameters. The perturbative stability of the models is also investigated through the squared sound speed.

state.text:
Title: PhOSv1: Efficient Scaling of Model Sleeping on a Single Server for Autoscaling with GPU-Context Deduplication

Abstract:
Autoscaling is a key mechanism in model-as-a-service systems, where fast scale-up is essential because the scale-up time directly determines how long a model service remains overloaded, which in turn governs serving quality. The state-of-the-art approach, model sleeping, adopted by mainstream serving engines including vLLM and SGLang, achieves near-zero-cost scale-up by pausing pre-spawned engines on the GPU. However, sleeping is not a free lunch: each sleeping model must keep its GPU context resident, and this cost grows linearly with the number of models, degrading serving performance. Because providers must support many models, they face a dilemma between fast scale-up for all models and high service performance. In this paper, we show that a single server can keep many models asleep without paying this GPU context tax. The key observation is that the contexts of sleeping models are largely duplicated: the driver (CUDA) context can be shared across models, and their GPU kernel binaries overlap heavily due to common operators and libraries. PhOSv1 deduplicates this context by transparently delegating each engine's GPU context allocation to a central daemon through API remoting; therefore, a single server can keep far more models asleep than current engines allow. Our evaluation shows that PhOSv1 matches the scale-up time of vanilla vLLM sleep mode while substantially reducing the GPU memory footprint, improving end-to-end multi-model serving performance.

Site: Stats Stack Exchange
Title: What is the effect on the statistics if the sample is almost the whole population?
Tags: hypothesis-testing, sample-size

Question:
Background: I am a mathematics school teacher and as part of that, I teach some basic statistics (UK A level maths & further maths for those that know). A key part of that is understanding hypothesis tests for a sample drawn from a population. One such is testing for zero correlation based on the correlation coefficient of a sample.

The issue of sample size arises in a qualitative sense: students know that the sample has to be "big enough" for the various approximations to apply but are only given some rough heuristics as to what "big enough" means.

What doesn't get addressed is what happens at the other end of the scale: what if the sample were almost the whole population?

I'm interested in the question as broadly as it can be interpreted, but I know that it is better here to narrow the question, so - if it helps - here's a more specific question.

Suppose I have bivariate data with a population size $N$, and I take a sample of size $n$. I measure the correlation coefficient, $r$, of the sample and run a hypothesis test to test if the correlation coefficient of the population, $\rho$, is $0$. To do this test, I would use a table of values which were - probably - generated from a Students t-distribution where the degrees of freedom depends on $n$. My understanding is that this distribution is chosen by assuming the sample is from a probability distribution which means a theoretically infinite population. That's fine if the actual population is large compared to the sample size. But what if not?

What happens to the validity of that hypothesis test as $n \to N$?

Answer A:
I would like to add a bit to the (good) answer by @[user], by introducing the term "superpopulation".

Let's use Thomas' example of pay discrimination at a university. To check this, I would define one (or probably more) "measures" of pay discrimination (e.g. pay difference between male and female staff with similar situations). I will then compute these measures. But since I have the full data, for all staff members over the last 30 years, I will obtain actual population measures, and I will express them w/o any "confidence intervals", or any other measure of uncertainty. They are the actual "truth".

But this population comes from a data generating process (DGP), and my population is just one possible realization of that DPG. Note that it is the only that will ever be; no other realization at that university over the last 30 years has ever happened, or will ever happen.

But if I am now testing if these measures give us some evidence of discrimination, I will now assume that this unique "population" I measured is actually a sample, from a virtually infinite superpopulation (i.e. from the DGP). Now that superpopulation is completely fictituous; it is purely a thought experiment. The only place they could have happened is in parallel universes. But that does matter...

I will run some statistical tests, on the measured parameters, as if they came from a sample, taken over this entirely imaginary, theoretical superpopulation. And I would not use any finite population correction (FPC).
[truncated]

Answer B:
We need to distinguish the concepts of the finite population and the data-generating process.

Suppose (to take a real example we use in class) you have complete data on salaries for all academics at a university for like 30 years.  The university is being sued for gender discrimination.  Does the fact you have complete data on the population mean you have zero uncertainty in your tests/estimates? No! The litigation isn't about the finite population, it's about the data-generating process: do men tend to get paid more than similarly situated women.  From this point of view there is randomness in the population. When you are doing hypothesis testing it is almost always testing hypotheses about the data-generating process.

Sometimes you are genuinely interested in the actual finite population. For example, many countries attempt to estimate the unemployment rate, which is a summary of the actual population of the country.  If you wanted to give an interval estimate of the unemployment rate, you would want take into account what proportion of the population you had sampled. If you had data for everyone (I don't know, maybe Vatican City does?) there would be no uncertainty in the estimated unemployment rate.

In practice, though, the pure sampling uncertainty in the national unemployment rate is small compared to non-sampling errors, and the sample is typically very much smaller than the population, so this doesn't matter.

It does matter in a few settings, where you really care about the actual population and you do a lot of sampling.  Statistics Canada does some surveys of First Nations people where the sampling rates for remote communities are quite high -- if you're going all the way to a small town in Nunavut, you might as well get the whole town's data.  Similarly, I know someone who is doing a survey of vision impairment in the Cook Islands,
[truncated]

Title: Linear hereditary quasirandomness

Abstract:
Conlon, Fox and Sudakov (\emph{Math. Proc. Cambridge Philos. Soc.} \textbf{164} (2018), 385--399) conjectured that hereditary subgraph counts force quasirandomness with linear dependence on the counting error. We prove this for every graph containing an edge. Let \(H\) have \(r\) vertices and \(m\ge1\) edges, and fix \(p\in(0,1)\). If every subset \(S\) of an \(n\)-vertex graph \(G\) contains \(p^m|S|^r\pmδn^r\) labelled injective copies of \(H\), then \(\lvert e_G(A,B)-p|A||B|\rvert\le C_{H,p}δn^2\) for all \(A,B\subseteq V(G)\), where \(e_G(A,B)\) counts ordered adjacent pairs. The proof extracts averaged rooted counts and represents each nonlinear term by a linear map in one selected edge factor. Composing two such maps gives an edge substitution with a superlinear cut-norm bound. A separate star expansion gives stronger local estimates for triangle-free graphs. The linear order is best possible even when \(2e(G)/n^2=p+O(n^{-2})\).

state.text:
Title: Learning to bid and bundle: a posterior-sampling agent for online retail

Abstract:
An online retailer launching a perishable product bids for sponsored-search clicks, discounts a bundle with an always-stocked staple and displays its remaining stock, which raises willingness to pay. It knows neither how clicks respond to its bid nor how strong and dispersed its market is, and learns both over repeated seasons from data its own decisions censor: a zero bid reveals nothing about paid clicks, and choices follow only clicks. We design a posterior-sampling agent for it. Each period it draws a market from an exact posterior and posts the bid and discount of that market's exactly solved season plan, so every action is one a fully informed seller could take. In a simulated online florist it has the lowest regret averaged over markets. In weak markets it gives up 12% to 23% of one season's revenue over 500 seasons, four to seven times less than drawing once per season. A planner acting on point estimates can stop bidding and never learn that bidding pays. The agent escapes after about three seasons on average, against fifty with one draw per season. Where displayed scarcity keeps willingness to pay above the posted price, the discount needs no learning. Customers waiting for the discount to return to its recent level look like lost sales, so frequent waiting makes the agent underrate its market. One discount per season removes waiting at a cost of 5.9% of clairvoyant revenue in a weak market and none in a strong one.

Brunel Medical School (BMS) is the medical school of Brunel University of London, a public research university in Uxbridge, west London, England. It offers a five-year Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery (MBBS) programme.

== History ==
Brunel Medical School was established as part of Brunel University of London's expansion into undergraduate medical education. Its MBBS programme began recruiting students for entry in 2022.

== Academic programmes ==
=== Undergraduate medicine ===
The school's principal programme is the five-year MBBS degree. The curriculum combines biomedical sciences, clinical skills, professional development and clinical placements.

== Teaching and learning ==
=== Team-based learning ===
Team-based learning is a principal teaching approach at the school. Students work in groups to apply medical knowledge and discuss clinical problems.

=== Clinical skills ===
Clinical and communication skills are incorporated throughout the programme, alongside simulation and supervised patient contact.

== Clinical training ==
Clinical placements take place in hospitals, general practices and community healthcare settings. The programme includes primary-care experiences and hospital-based clinical training.

== Facilities ==
Medical teaching takes place on Brunel University's campus, using anatomy teaching facilities, clinical skills laboratories and simulated hospital wards.

== Student support ==
The school operates a House system, with students allocated to one of five Houses.

== Accreditation and regulation ==
Medical education in the United Kingdom is regulated by the General Medical Council. The programme's current regulatory status should be verified against the latest published GMC and university information.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Orders of outer automorphisms of $S_6$
Tags: group-theory, symmetric-groups, automorphism-group

Question:
It is known that the only symmetric group $S_n$ that has an outer automorphism is the case where $n=6$.

The order of a permutation in $S_6$ (and hence also of its corresponding inner automorphism) is given by the lcm of its disjoint cycle lengths. Hence, the order may be $1, 2, 3, 4, 5,$ or $6$.

If $f$ is an outer automorphism of $S_6$, then $f^2$ is an inner automorphism (because the outer automorphism group of $S_6$ is cyclic of order $2$), hence the order of $f^2$ must be $1, 2, 3, 4, 5,$ or $6$. Also, the order of $f$ must be even for the same reason, hence it must be twice the order of $f^2$. This means that the order of $f$ must be $2, 4, 6, 8, 10,$ or $12$.

But do all six potential orders of outer automorphisms of $S_6$ actually occur? The order $2$ case is known to be possible (see An Example of Outer Automorphism of $S_6$ with order 2?), so it remains to check the other five potential orders.

== Yaser S. Natour (Professor in Speech and Language Pathology) ==
Yaser Natour (Al-Natour) is a Jordanian Speech and Language Pathologist and academic. Whose work has focused on voice disorders, swallowing disorders (dysphagia), resonance and neurogenic disorders. He was born in Amman - Jordan (26 July 1969), Yaser was one of (seven) children from a working-class family.

== Education and Academic Career ==
Natour got his Bachelor Degree(B.A.) in 1991, and Masters in Speech Pathology and Communication Disorders in 1997 from University of Jordan followed by a (Ph.D) in Communication Sciences and Disorders from University of Florida in 2001.

He later held acadimc and clinical positions in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates. In 2013, "The National" [ref: UAE University takes lead in disability care, The National] reported that Natour was managing a newly established Assessment and treatment unit at United Arab Emirates University. In 2015, "Al- Ittihad" reported that the unit had provided assessment and treatment services to more than 200 clients. [ref: علاج 200 طفل من مشاكل النطق بجامعة الإمارات]

He subsequently held academic appointments in speech- language pathology at the University of Jordan, [ref: Request Rejected, rehabilitation.ju.edu.jo] and other institutions in the region.

== Clinical and Community Initiatives ==
Natour has been associated with the University of Jordan teletherapy group, and Initiative providing remote speech, language and hearing rehabilitation services. In December 2015 independent Jordanian education news outlet “Talaba News” reported that the group was led by and that is provided remote rehabilitation services for people with speech and language disorders. [ref: الجامعة الأردنيّة تتصدّر جائزة الحسين بن عبد الله الثّاني للعمل التطوعيّ لعام 2025 وتظفر بجائزتين, Talaba News]

In 2025, the group received first place in the team category of the AlHussein Bin Abdullah II Award for Voluntary Service. [ref: ولي العهد يكرم الفائزين بجائزة الحسين بن عبدالله الثاني للعمل التطوعي في دورتها الثالثة, News Agency (Petra)]

== Research and Publications ==
Natour's research has addressed voice assessment, dysphagia and speech and language disorders.

In 2010, Ahmad F. Saleem and Natour published a validation study of the Arabic version of the Voice Handicap Index. [ref: Standardization of the Arabic version of the Voice Handicap Index: an investigation of validity and reliability, Logopedics, Phoniatrics, Vocology] The study reported the Arabic version to be a valid speaking instrument for assessing the effects of the voice disorders among Arabic speaking patients.
