state.text:
Title: A 211K Parameter Foundation Model: Genetic Prompting in Neural Cellular Automata

Abstract:
The scale of modern foundation models enables broad task generalization. In medical imaging, where segmentation demands vary widely across clinical contexts, such flexibility is invaluable. But current models, such as SAM trade adaptability for scale, locking their utility behind high-end infrastructure and leaving behind the low-resource environments most in need of diagnostic support. To bridge this gap, we introduce Foundational-NCA, a lightweight foundation model capable of adapting to a wide range of medical segmentation tasks without retraining. Built on Neural Cellular Automata (NCA), Foundational-NCA incorporates gradient-based learning with genetic optimization over a latent task space, using a compact task vector to guide predictions. This enables dynamic adaptation via a genetic prompt mechanism, allowing the model to generalize across tasks while keeping the parameter count magnitudes lower at just 211 thousand, compared to SAM-based models with 38.9 to 636 million parameters. We evaluate Foundational-NCA on 15 trained and 6 entirely unseen segmentation tasks from the TotalSegmentator dataset, achieving an average Dice score of 84.5% on known tasks and 60.4% on unseen ones. These results demonstrate that task generalization is possible in ultra-compact models, laying the groundwork for resource-efficient, deployable foundation models in clinical environments where infrastructure is limited. By reducing model size by over 180 times, Foundational-NCA takes a step toward a more equitable future for medical AI, one where powerful tools are within reach of every healthcare setting.

Title: Taylor-type joint spectrum and essential spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators

Abstract:
As the cornerstone of multivariable operator theory, (essential) Taylor's joint spectrum plays crucial roles in many areas. The present paper is devoted to developing the theory of (essential) Taylor-type joint spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators on Hilbert spaces and to establishing the associated Fredholm index theory. Furthermore, the holomorphic functional calculus for row-bounded sequences is established. At last, we obtain a Gleason-Richter-Sundberg type index theorem in the infinite-variable setting, which connects the Fredholm index, the asymptotic Arveson's curvature invariant and fibre dimensions.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Robert Van Gulick

Draft text:
----

----

Robert Van Gulick is a philosopher and professor of philosophy at Syracuse University. [ref: Robert Van Gulick, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences] His work is primarily in the philosophy of mind and philosophy of cognitive science, particularly consciousness, self-awareness and functionalism. [ref: Robert N. Van Gulick Curriculum Vitae, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences]

Van Gulick is associated with the Higher-Order Global States (HOGS) model of consciousness, which combines elements of higher-order and global-state approaches to conscious awareness. [ref: Higher-Order Theories of Consciousness] [ref: Consciousness] The model has subsequently been discussed in academic literature on higher-order and self-representational theories of consciousness. [ref: Same old, same old: the same-order representation theory of consciousness and the division of phenomenal labor, Synthese] [ref: Phenomenal consciousness with infallible self-representation, Philosophical Studies] [ref: The Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Consciousness, Oxford University Press]

== Education and career ==

Van Gulick received an A.B. in philosophy from Princeton University in 1970. He earned an M.A. in 1973 and a Ph.D. in philosophy in 1976 from the University of California, Berkeley. His dissertation was titled Functionalism as a Theory of Mind.

He taught at Rutgers University from 1976 to 1984 and joined Syracuse University in 1984. He became a professor of philosophy at Syracuse in 1995. From 2008 to 2010, he held Syracuse's William P. Tolley Distinguished Teaching Professorship in the Humanities. [ref: William P. Tolley Distinguished Teaching Professor in the Humanities, Syracuse University College of Arts and Sciences]

Van Gulick served as president of the Society for Philosophy and Psychology in 2002. [ref: Past Officers, Society for Philosophy and Psychology]

== Philosophical work ==

Van Gulick has written on consciousness, self-awareness, functionalism, intentionality, emergence and the relationship between phenomenal experience and cognitive organization.

=== Higher-Order Global States ===

Van Gulick developed the Higher-Order Global States model as an account of the relationship between consciousness and higher-order awareness. In contrast to standard higher-order accounts that posit a distinct higher-order representation of a lower-order mental state, HOGS treats the relevant higher-order content as arising within the organization of a larger global state.

The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy interprets Van Gulick's account as one in which globally available first-order states acquire a higher-order dimension through their incorporation into representations of the self and its relationship to the environment. It also notes some ambiguity in the theory concerning the precise relationship between the original first-order state and the resulting higher-order global state.

The HOGS model has been discussed in subsequent work on higher-order and self-representational theories of consciousness. Josh Weisberg examined the model in Synthese as a form of same-order representation theory and considered its combination of global availability and self-awareness. Chad Kidd considered HOGS alongside other self-representational models in Philosophical Studies, including whether its account of integrated conscious states addresses problems involving self-misrepresentation.

Tom McClelland discusses HOGS in The Oxford Handbook of the Philosophy of Consciousness, situating it within self-representational theories and describing the role that integration into a subject's broader mental economy plays in the account. Later authors have continued to compare aspects of HOGS with alternative accounts of higher-order representation and self-consciousness. [ref: Quotational higher-order thought theory, Philosophical Studies] [ref: Pre-Reflective Self-Consciousness: A Meta-Causal Approach, Review of Philosophy and Psychology]

Van Gulick later connected HOGS with Global Neuronal Workspace theory. In an editorial introducing a 2022 special issue on self-consciousness, Stefan Lang and Klaus Viertbauer describe his contribution as combining HOGS with the Global Neuronal Workspace framework and developing a virtual-self integration account of the conscious subject. [ref: Editorial: Self-Consciousness Explained—Mapping the Field, Review of Philosophy and Psychology]

Title: Lifting mod $p$ Galois representations over local fields

Abstract:
Let $K$ be a local field with absolute Galois group $G_{K}$ and let $k$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$. We prove that every continuous representation $G_K\to \operatorname{GL}_{n}(k)$ lifts to a continuous representation $G_K\to\operatorname{GL}_{n}(W(k))$ where $W(k)$ is the ring of infinite Witt vectors over $k$.

Site: Math Stack Exchange
Title: Zeros of $1 - \frac{\Gamma(x - \frac{z}{2})}{\Gamma(\frac{z}{2})}$ on the line $\text{Re}(z) = x$
Tags: complex-analysis, analytic-number-theory, gamma-function, riemann-zeta

Question:
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and define
$$
f(z,x)=\frac{\Gamma\left(x-\frac{z}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{z}{2}\right)}
$$

Is it possible to prove that, for every $x \in \mathbb{R}$, the function $1-f(z,x)$ has infinitely many zeros on the vertical line $\operatorname{Re}(z)=x$, i.e., at points $z=x+it$ with $t \in \mathbb{R}$?

This is motivated by the Riemann zeta functional equation, which uses this exact ratio for $x = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$ \zeta(z) = \pi^{z-\frac{1}{2}} \frac{\Gamma\left(\frac{1}{2}-\frac{z}{2}\right)}{\Gamma\left(\frac{z}{2}\right)} \zeta(1-z) $$

Site: Physics Stack Exchange
Title: Does power equal momentum times acceleration?
Tags: forces, momentum, power

Question:
This might be a bit of a mundane question but I need help to resolve a question that came up in a discussion with a friend in our physics class.

My friend claimed that because $P=\mathbf{Fv}$, it also equals m$\mathbf{av}$, and from this you can get $P=\mathbf{pa}$, since momentum ($\mathbf{p}$) equals $m\mathbf{v}$. I feel like this shouldn't work in practice, but I can't find anything online to concretely dispel (or perhaps prove) this relation true or false.

My friend also claims that this equation would work for a variable force/mass (which was my original objection) since you can turn it into a differential equation with functions, which he showed me. I don't know enough to figure out whether you can actually do this, so I came here.

I would greatly appreciate if someone could help me out with this!

Answer A:
In Newton mechanics, the time derivative of the kinetic energy is $$\frac{d~}{dt} \frac{mv^2}{2} = {\bf p \cdot a}~.$$ It is not true for the relativistic energy, for which $$\frac{dm\gamma}{dt} = m\gamma^3 {\bf v \cdot a}~.$$

Answer B:
My friend claimed that because $P=\mathbf{Fv}$, it also equals m$\mathbf{av}$, and from this you can get $P=\mathbf{pa}$,

The relationship ${\bf F} = m {\bf a}$ (Newton's second law) only holds when $\bf F$ is the net force.  You are substituting in for $\bf F$ with $m{\bf a}$ in order to obtain $P={\bf p}\cdot{\bf a}$, which is only correct when ${\bf F}$ is the net force.

If you are interested in the power due to the net force acting over some distance, then you can use either of the equations you (or your friend) suggest. Each is (fairly trivially) related to the other equation by Newton's second law.

I feel like this shouldn't work in practice

It will work if $\bf F$ is the net force. Otherwise it will generally not work.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Okko The Exiled

Draft text:
----

Okko The Exiled is an action-adventure platform game developed by Frozen Flame Interactive and published by Eastasiasoft Limited. The game was released for Windows and macOS on September 30, 2026, with console versions planned for 2027. [ref: Gorgeously animated 2D action-adventure Okko The Exiled is OUT NOW for PC, eastasiasoft]

The game is set in Kutala, a land inhabited by demons, and follows Okko, who sets out to defeat the Demon Lord Yalda and fulfill an ancient oath. [ref: Okko The Exiled, Steam]

== Gameplay ==
Okko The Exiled is a 2D side-scrolling action-adventure game featuring platforming, real-time combat and exploration. Players control Okko as he travels through Kutala, fighting enemies and bosses while acquiring new abilities. [ref: Okko The Exiled, eastasiasoft]

The game features hand-drawn pixel-art animation, combat abilities that allow Okko to stomp, launch and deflect enemies, and a hub area known as the Old Throne. Players can also collect Deevols, which unlock additional challenge levels.

Reviews have described the game as a 2D action platformer with some Metroidvania-style progression and an emphasis on exploration and secrets. [ref: Review: Okko the Exiled, Movies, Games and Tech]

== Plot ==
The game is set in Kutala, a land of demons ruled by the Demon Lord Yalda. Okko is a young horned demon who has spent much of his life isolated from the wider world. He eventually sets out on a quest that involves defeating the rulers of Kutala and fulfilling an ancient oath. [ref: Análise: Okko The Exiled não revoluciona, mas traz uma bela e satisfatória experiência de ação 2D, GameBlast]

== Development ==
Okko The Exiled was developed by independent studio Frozen Flame Interactive in cooperation with Eastasiasoft. Frozen Flame Interactive was founded by Matthew Strnad, who had previously developed the platform game Robozarro. [ref: Pixel art action platformer Okko The Exiled arrives on consoles and PC in late 2025, eastasiasoft]

The game was presented at the Tokyo Game Show in 2025 and subsequently featured a playable demo during Steam Next Fest.

== Release ==
Okko The Exiled was released digitally for Windows and macOS through Steam and GOG.com on September 30, 2026. The standard edition was priced at US$14.99, while a deluxe edition containing the digital soundtrack was priced at US$19.99.

Console versions for PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch, Xbox One and Xbox Series X/S are planned for early 2027.

== Reception ==
Okko The Exiled received generally positive reviews from critics, who praised its pixel-art presentation, animation, combat, boss encounters, progression system and musical score. Criticism focused primarily on aspects of its controls, platforming, puzzles and level design. [ref: Review: Okko the Exiled, Movies, Games and Tech] [ref: Okko The Exiled – Recensione PC, GameSource] [ref: Análise: Okko The Exiled não revoluciona, mas traz uma bela e satisfatória experiência de ação 2D, GameBlast] [ref: Okko The Exiled, Pizza Fria] [ref: Review – Okko The Exiled, Gamestic] [ref: Okko The Exiled Steam Review – Welcomed Home Or Sent Away?, Retro News]

Movies, Games & Tech and GameSource both rated the game 7 out of 10. Movies, Games & Tech praised its level design, secrets and boss encounters, while criticizing aspects of its controls and traversal mechanics. GameSource highlighted the combat system, progression and visual presentation, while criticizing the predictability of some enemies and aspects of the game's movement and Focus Mode.

GameBlast gave the game 7.5 out of 10, praising its controls, character mobility, pixel art, boss fights and story, while finding that some mechanics were underused and that certain levels were unnecessarily prolonged. Pizza Fria rated the game 6.5 out of 10, praising its visual presentation and progression while criticizing the long levels, repetitive use of the soundtrack and some platforming mechanics.

Gamestic gave a cautiously positive assessment, praising the hand-drawn pixel art, animations, character designs, soundtrack and boss encounters. The review criticized the controls during tight platforming sections and described several progression puzzles as unclear. The reviewer reported encountering softlocks that could be resolved by reloading the game. They also noted that the soundtrack is impressive, though could become repetitive because the same track is used across two full stages.

Retro News gave a strongly positive assessment, praising the game's level structure, secrets, difficulty curve, combat system, pixel art, animation and soundtrack. The review described the gameplay and presentation as excellent and considered the game a strong value for its price, recommending it to action-platformer fans.

Title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information

Abstract:
The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

state.text:
Title: On a positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham for Padé approximants to the matrix exponential

Abstract:
We study the positivity conjecture of Fasi and Higham [SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 40 (2019), Conjecture 3.2], which concerns the Taylor coefficients of the reciprocal of the denominator $q_{k,m}(z)$ of the Padé approximant to the matrix exponential. The conjecture asserts that these coefficients are positive whenever $m$ is odd. We prove full positivity for $k=0$ and eventual positivity whenever the unique positive real zero of $q_{k,m}$ is the unique zero of minimal modulus. We also give an explicit computable sufficient threshold beyond which all coefficients are positive. Using Hermite scaling with leading-coefficient normalization, we prove that this spectral minimality holds for each fixed odd $m$ and all sufficiently large $k$. The unrestricted conjecture is nevertheless false. We give exact rational counterexamples and prove a transient scaling theorem showing that on the scale $n\asymp\sqrt{k+1}$ the normalized coefficients converge to an explicit oscillatory Hermite profile. For $m=5$ this profile is negative at one point, yielding infinitely many counterexamples. The counterexamples are not diagonal, and the diagonal case $k=m$, which is the case relevant in practice, remains open. These results do not imply a failure of the Fasi--Higham algorithm. Rather, they delimit the range in which the auxiliary positivity conjecture can be used as a theorem.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Deep Structure Theory

Draft text:
Deep Structure Theory (DST), also known as Neuropsychological Deep Structure Theory, is a unifying analytical framework that models how mental states emerge as compiled electromagnetic oscillatory activity relating to the structure and function of underlying neural circuitry. It is a local instance of dynamic complex systems theory that applies to how the brain generates the mind and was introduced by the cognitive neuroscientist and psychotherapy researcher Oliver Boxell. [ref: Deep Structure Theory: An introduction to a unifying theoretical framework for the analysis of human neuropsychology., Journal of Mind and Behavior]

The term "deep structure" was popularized in formal linguistics by Noam Chomsky in his theory of generative grammar, although this referred only to a core syntactic structure that could be expressed as different surface sentence forms. Boxell radically extends and deepens the idea in DST by developing it into a standard model for the entirety of the mind in which core conceptual meaning representations can be re-coded into integrated language, mathematics, music and sound patterns, or visuospatial and sensorimotor patterns. Furthermore, while Chomsky viewed mental representation in isolation, DST describes deep structure as the product of integrated, co-evolved representational and real-time processing subsystems. As such, the DST paradigm is able to stipulate systems for memory, learning, and sustained developmental patterns over time, in which the emergence of consciousness appears and plays a mediating role. The relationship between micro- and macro- neural circuits and compiled oscillations as the encoding of deep structure also makes DST more explicit about how the mind emerges from the structure and function of the brain, although generative grammar also more loosely viewed deep structure as somehow relating to the structure of the brain.

=== Basic Technical Outline ===
Universal deep structure algorithms: Boxell imports three core algorithms from X-Bar Theory (namely the complement, specifier, and adjunct rules), as well as binary switches, but views them as domain-general faculty for core meaning rather than a language-specific one. As such, in DST these formal algorithms derive abstract mental information structure as encoded by compiled neural oscillations. In common with dynamic complex systems theories generally, these neurosymbolic structures are computed as branching computations of nodes (units of information) that form binary tree representations.

Phase transitions: The domain-general faculty for core meaning occurs in the Information-Phase (I-Phase) of deep structural computation. One of the main functions of the I-Phase is conceptual or thematic role assignment, in which the deep structural tree incorporates theta theory and predicate logic. As some of these I-Phase computations reach a neural activation threshold filter known as theta (Φ) they transition into the Spellout-Phase (S-Phase), where the core meaning derivations are re-rendered into modality-specific deep structural forms through the addition of abstract features to the nodes, producing language, mathematics, music and sound patterning, and visuospatial and sensorimotor patterning. The I-to-S phase transitions in DST subsume transformations and phase analysis from the Minimalist Program and extend it as per-propositional chunking to all neurocognitive domains as a general computational working memory constraint.

Linearization: Some I-Phase and especially S-Phase computations reach another neural threshold filter called omega (Ω) that precipitates the deletion of branches from the deep structural tree representations to create a linear string of nodes. Subsets of deep structures that undergo this transition become self-aware or conscious, in-line with fundamental neurobiological research on consciousness that finds it appears when activation thresholds are reached in conjunction with highly distributed macrocircuits. [ref: What is the readiness potential?, Trends in Cognitive Sciences] [ref: Unconscious determinants of free decisions in the human brain, Nature Neuroscience] [ref: Piercing of Consciousness as a Threshold-Crossing Operation, Current Biology] [ref: Neural correlates of evidence accumulation during value-based decisions revealed via simultaneous EEG-fMRI, Nature Communications]

Memory: The sustained strength of transient neural circuit structures upregulates the strength of branch connections between nodes in deep structural tree derivations. Using Marvin Minsky's typology, Boxell calls the strength of branch connections "k-lines" (knowledge lines). [ref: K-Lines: A theory of memory, Cognitive Science] Just as neural circuits upregulate k-lines, k-line strengths can downregulate neural circuit connectivity strength; at both the neurobiological and emergent neuropsychological levels, frequency, recency, and saliency are proposed as the main filters that determine connectivity strengths. The ephemeral nature of k-lines show how the processing subsystem is instrumental in forming part of the nature of the deep structures that are built along with the actual representational algorithms that constrain their nature.

Title: A Neural Network Approach towards Real-Time Knot Point Density Estimates for the Nonlinear Quadrotor

Abstract:
Spline representations provide a compact way to approximate continuous trajectories using a finite number of parameters. When approximating trajectories generated by dynamical systems, the efficiency of a spline representation depends strongly on the placement of knot points. Uniform knot distributions often lead to inefficient representations, requiring either unnecessary control points or producing poor approximations in regions where the trajectory varies rapidly. In this work we propose a learning-based method for adaptive knot placement in B-spline approximations of trajectories generated by ordinary differential equations. A neural network learns a mapping from the initial condition of the system to quantities that characterize the local variation of the resulting trajectory. These estimates are used to construct nonuniform knot distributions that approximately equidistribute a local error indicator, reducing the number of control points needed to meet a prescribed accuracy.

state.text:
Title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians

Abstract:
Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $γ$ with a $K$-orbit $κ$, and $M=κ\capγ$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $γ$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $κ$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.

Title: MFRC522 RFID Reader Works Intermittently with ESP32
Tags: esp32, rfid, micropython, mfrc522

Question:
I'm working on a project using the MFRC522 RFID reader module, but I'm experiencing an intermittent issue. Sometimes the reader works correctly and detects RFID cards, while other times it fails to detect them. I've already implemented the RFID functionality using the existing library, so I'm trying to identify the cause of this intermittent behavior.

Hardware:

Microcontroller:  ESP32

RFID reader: RC522

Power supply: 3V3

What i saw:

The reader works correctly sometimes when my teammate held it.

When i hold it, it received power, the light was red but i don't see any card.

Since it's read the cards sometimes, i  think my wiring wasn't the problem.

My code:

from machine import Pin, SPI
import time

# ESP32 + RC522
CS_PIN = 5
RST_PIN = 27

spi = SPI(
    2,
    baudrate=100000,
    polarity=0,
    phase=0,
    bits=8,
    firstbit=SPI.MSB,
    sck=Pin(18),
    mosi=Pin(23),
    miso=Pin(19)
)

cs = Pin(CS_PIN, Pin.OUT, value=1)
rst = Pin(RST_PIN, Pin.OUT, value=1)

# =========================
# RC522 REGISTER
# =========================
CommandReg = 0x01
ComIEnReg = 0x02
ComIrqReg = 0x04
ErrorReg = 0x06
FIFODataReg = 0x09
FIFOLevelReg = 0x0A
ControlReg = 0x0C
BitFramingReg = 0x0D
ModeReg = 0x11
TxControlReg = 0x14
TxASKReg = 0x15
CRCResultRegH = 0x21
CRCResultRegL = 0x22
TModeReg = 0x2A
TPrescalerReg = 0x2B
TReloadRegH = 0x2C
TReloadRegL = 0x2D
VersionReg = 0x37

PCD_IDLE = 0x00
PCD_TRANSCEIVE = 0x0C
PCD_SOFTRESET = 0x0F

PICC_REQIDL = 0x26
PICC_ANTICOLL = 0x93

# SPI REGISTER ACCESS
def write_reg(reg, value):
    cs.value(0)
    spi.write(bytes([(reg << 1) & 0x7E, value & 0xFF]))
    cs.value(1)

def read_reg(reg):
    cs.value(0)
    spi.write(bytes([((reg << 1) & 0x7E) | 0x80]))
    value = spi.read(1, 0x00)[0]
    cs.value(1)
    return value

def set_mask(reg, mask):
    write_reg(reg, read_reg(reg) | mask)

def clear_mask(reg, mask):
    write_reg(reg, read_reg(reg) & (~mask & 0xFF))

# RESET + INITIALIZATION
def reset_reader():
    rst.value(0)
    time.sleep_ms(10)
    rst.value(1)
    time.sleep_ms(50)

    write_reg(CommandReg, PCD_SOFTRESET)
    time.sleep_ms(50)

    write_reg(TModeReg, 0x8D)
    write_reg(TPrescalerReg, 0x3E)
    write_reg(TReloadRegL, 30)
    write_reg(TReloadRegH, 0)
    write_reg(TxASKReg, 0x40)
    write_reg(ModeReg, 0x3D)

    # Bat anten RFID
    set_mask(TxControlReg, 0x03)

def calculate_crc(data):
    write_reg(CommandReg, PCD_IDLE)
    write_reg(FIFOLevelReg, 0x80)

    for byte in data:
        write_reg(FIFODataReg, byte)

    write_reg(CommandReg, 0x03)

    for _ in range(100):
        if read_reg(0x05) & 0x04:
            break
        time.sleep_ms(1)

    return [
        read_reg(CRCResultRegL),
        read_reg(CRCResultRegH)
    ]

# SEND COMMAND TO CARD
def communicate(command, data, tx_last_bits=0):
    write_reg(CommandReg, PCD_IDLE)
    write_reg(ComIrqReg, 0x7F)
    write_reg(FIFOLevelReg, 0x80)

    for byte in data:
        write_reg(FIFODataReg, byte)

    write_reg(BitFramingReg, tx_last_bits)
    write_reg(CommandReg, command)

    if command == PCD_TRANSCEIVE:
        set_mask(BitFramingReg, 0x80)

    irq = 0
    for _ in range(100):
        irq = read_reg(ComIrqReg)
        if irq & 0x30 or irq & 0x01:
            break
        time.sleep_ms(1)

    clear_mask(BitFramingReg, 0x80)

    if irq & 0x01:
        return False, []

    if read_reg(ErrorReg) & 0x1B:
        return False, []

    count = read_reg(FIFOLevelReg)
    last_bits = read_reg(ControlReg) & 0x07

    if count == 0:
        return True, []

    if count > 16:
        return False, []

    result = [read_reg(FIFODataReg) for _ in range(count)]
    return True, result

# REQUEST CARD
def request_card():
    write_reg(BitFramingReg, 0x07)
    ok, response = communicate(
        PCD_TRANSCEIVE, [PICC_REQIDL], 7
    )

    if ok and len(response) == 2:
        return True

    return False
# READ UID
def read_uid():
    write_reg(BitFramingReg, 0x00)

    ok, data = communicate(
        PCD_TRANSCEIVE, [PICC_ANTICOLL, 0x20]
    )

    if not ok or len(data) != 5:
        return None

    checksum = data[0] ^ data[1] ^ data[2] ^ data[3]

    if checksum != data[4]:
        return None

    return data[:4]

# MAIN
print("\n=== RC522 STANDALONE TEST ===")

reset_reader()
time.sleep_ms(50)

version = read_reg(VersionReg)
print("VersionReg =", hex(version))

if version not in (0x91, 0x92):
    print("Warning: Version is not common.")
    print("Checking SPI, power and wiring.")

print("Bring the card close to RC522...\n")

last_uid = None

while True:
    try:
        if request_card():
            uid = read_uid()

            if uid is not None:
                uid_text = "".join(
                    "{:02X}".format(b) for b in uid
                )

                if uid_text != last_uid:
                    print("Successfully read")
                    print("UID:", uid_text)
                    print("--------------------")
                    last_uid = uid_text

        else:
            last_uid = None

        time.sleep_ms(100)

    except Exception as e:
        print("RFID error:", e)
        time.sleep_ms(500)

----

Yang Jung-won (Korean: 양정원; born February 9, 2004), known mononymously as Jungwon, is a South Korean singer, dancer, and the leader of the K-pop boy band Enhypen. Appointed to the leadership role at age 16, he drew media attention for being one of the youngest group leaders in the music industry. [ref: Youngest leaders taking charge in K-pop industry, The Korea Herald]

== Early life and education ==
Jungwon practiced Taekwondo for seven years prior to his training in the entertainment industry. [ref: Jungwon Weverse Magazine Interview, Weverse Magazine] He attended Namgang High School before transferring to Hanlim Multi Art School, where he graduated from the Department of Practical Dance in February 2023. He trained under SM Entertainment and Big Hit Music before joining Belift Lab.

== Career ==
=== 2020–present: Debut with Enhypen ===
In June 2020, Jungwon was introduced as a contestant on the reality survival competition show I-Land, created by CJ ENM and Big Hit Entertainment. [ref: 'I-LAND' unveils full lineup of 23 trainees, Newsen] During the live finale on September 18, 2020, he placed first in the global viewer voting with 1,417,620 votes, securing his spot in the final lineup of the boy band Enhypen. [ref: 'Global fan-made band' Enhypen debuts with album 'Border: Day One', Korea JoongAng Daily]

Following a comprehensive 40-day selection process that included interviews with staff and members, Jungwon was officially announced as the leader of the group on November 13, 2020. [ref: Enhypen selects Jungwon as group leader, newsen] Appointed to the position at 16 years old, his selection drew significant media attention as it made him one of the youngest group leaders in modern K-pop history, leading a team where the majority of the members were older than him. [ref: Jungwon chosen as leader, The Korea Herald]

=== Other activities ===
==== Hosting ====
Beyond his group activities, Jungwon has taken on solo hosting responsibilities. He served as a regular radio host (MC) for the Educational Broadcasting System (EBS) program Listen, co-hosting the weekly broadcast alongside fellow group member Sunoo. [ref: ENHYPEN Jungwon and Sunoo selected as new DJs for EBS radio 'Listen', Ilsan Sports]

==== Ambassadorships ====
On April 17, 2026, the Seoul Metropolitan Government officially appointed Yang Jungwon as an honorary ambassador for the 2026 Seoul International Garden Show held at Seoul Forest. [ref: Enhypen's Jungwon named honorary ambassador for Seoul International Garden Show, Korea JoongAng Daily] [ref: Enhypen's Jungwon named ambassador for Seoul International Garden Show, The Korea Herald] His appointment was heavily publicized due to his name being a homonym for the Korean word for "garden" (jeongwon). In this civic role, he was tasked with promoting urban sustainability and green initiatives through promotional videos and public audio guides for visitors.

As a member of Enhypen, Jungwon has also participated in several major global group brand ambassadorships, including Italian luxury fashion house Prada, Dunkin' Philippines, and Samyang Foods' MEP ramyeon campaign.

==== Recording Academy membership ====
In July 2025, Jungwon was invited to join The Recording Academy as a voting member for its 2025 class, granting voting rights for the 68th Annual Grammy Awards. [ref: Recording Academy Welcomes New Member Class Of 2025, The Recording Academy] [ref: Hybe CEO Lee Jae-sang named professional member of The Recording Academy, The Korea Herald] [ref: 16 K-pop artists, producers under HYBE added to Grammy Awards voting members list, Korea JoongAng Daily] The Academy highlighted his artistic contributions as a singer, dancer, and leader of Enhypen, alongside his budding songwriting work on tracks such as "Highway 1009" and "Hundred Broken Hearts."

Title: Intuition for method of characteristics in Burgers’ equation and shock formation
Tags: fluid-dynamics, non-linear-systems, shock-waves

Question:
I am trying to understand the method of characteristics in the context of the inviscid Burgers’ equation

$$
\frac{\partial u}{\partial t} + u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x} = 0.
$$

I think I understand the general idea that the nonlinear term $u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}$ causes different parts of the wave to travel at different speeds, which leads to wave steepening.

My understanding is that this eventually leads to a situation where the solution would have multiple values at the same point in space, which is not physically possible, so a discontinuity must form.

I have read that the method of characteristics is what is used to analyse this and explain shock formation, but I do not really understand what the method is actually doing or what the characteristic curves represent physically.

Am I thinking about this correctly, and can someone explain in an intuitive way how the method of characteristics leads to this picture of wave steepening and shock formation?

Title: What factor is more important in determining sample size?
Tags: sampling

Question:
Given a statistical model $M(\theta_1,\dots,\theta_p)$.

Assuming a true value of each $\theta_i$ is known, via simulation, I can determine two different sample sizes:

Parameter Recovery: The $n$ needed so that each estimate $\hat\theta_i$ falls within $\pm k\%$ of its true value with probability at least $q$ .

Coverage: The $n$ needed so that a 95% confidence interval for the estimated mean of $M$ (i.e. $\mathbb{E}_M[Y]$) contains the true mean a proportion $j$ of the time (coverage of the derived quantity $g(\theta) = \mathbb{E}_M[Y]$).

Which of these is typically the more important factor/target when choosing $n$?

state.text:
Title: Hook monomial immanants are Kazhdan-Lusztig positive

Abstract:
Stembridge conjectured that every monomial immanant is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices, and Haiman proposed a stronger statement which at $q=1$ says that every monomial immanant is a non-negative integer combination of the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanants of Rhoades and Skandera. We prove this for every hook shape $(a,1^{n-a})$ and every $n$. More precisely, each of the per-vertex functions obtained by splitting Stembridge's formula for hook characters is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive. The main tool is a positivity statement for products: a product of Kazhdan-Lusztig positive immanants of complementary submatrices is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive, which we deduce at $q=1$ from Braden's hyperbolic localization, following Billey and Braden. With Haiman's theorem for irreducible characters, it shows that every class function whose Frobenius characteristic lies in the semiring generated by Schur functions and hook monomial symmetric functions is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive; for example, Skandera's chain of normalised hook immanants is Kazhdan-Lusztig positive for every $n$. We place these results in a comparison of three cones of class functions, and show that the remaining obstructions to Haiman's conjecture lie at singular Schubert varieties that are not reached by an iterated doubling identity of Abreu and Nigro, for which we give an explicit criterion. Finally, on the full span of permutation monomials, an element that is non-negative on totally non-negative matrices can have a negative coefficient at the Kazhdan-Lusztig immanant $\mathrm{Imm}_w$ if and only if the Schubert variety $X_w$ is singular; Skandera proved the smooth half.

Title: A lifted entropy splitting lemma and applications

Abstract:
We give a matrix lifting of the entropy-splitting theorem of Csiszár, Körner, Lovász, Marton, and Simonyi, and show several applications. We use it to prove the Cartesian-product inequality conjectured by Sinjorgo and Sotirov for the generalized Lovász theta number, and we also answer the saturation and convexification questions of Carli Silva, Coutinho, Oliveira, and Tunçel on the same theme. For the strong Hoffman bound, we answer a question of Wocjan, Elphick, and Darbari concerning orthogonal rank, and show that optimization over matrix weights gives exactly the ceiling of the theta number of the complement. Finally, we extend the lifting to diagonally invariant cones of positive semidefinite matrices, giving a proof of a conjecture by Kuryatnikova, Sotirov, and Vera, and giving a short proof, for all graphs, of a theta-based weakening of Fajtlowicz's graph-energy conjecture.

Wiki: English Wikipedia
Draft: Of Woman Born: Motherhood as Experience & Institution

Draft text:
Of Woman Born: Motherhood as Experience and Institution is a 1976 book by American poet, scholar, and essayist Adrienne Rich that examines motherhood from the lens of personal experience, anthropology, and feminist theory. Rich researched and wrote the book over a 4 year period because she felt that motherhood “was a crucial, still relatively unexplored, area for feminist theory.” [ref: Of woman born: motherhood as experience and institution, W. W. Norton & Company] It has been described by the Los Angeles Times as a landmark work in the literature of motherhood. [ref: Adrienne Rich dies at 82; feminist poet and essayist, Los Angeles Times]

== Summary ==

Of Woman Born begins with a foreword describing one of the book’s central aims: to begin to fill in the gap between the universal experience of motherhood and what is known about it: “We know more about the air we breathe, the seas we travel, than about the nature and meaning of motherhood.” The foreword also describes the book’s aim to create a distinction between motherhood as an experience, which Rich defines as “the potential relationship of any woman to her powers of reproduction and to children” and motherhood as an institution—the social and political systems that define, limit, and control the experience of motherhood.

=== Anger and Tenderness ===
Using entries from her journal, Rich illustrates the conflicting feelings she experienced as a young mother of three in the 1950’s: tenderness and anger, ambition and weariness, power and powerlessness. She describes how, from an early age,  she struggled to bridge the gap between the feminine ideals of the 1950’s, and her own vision of herself as a serious, independent poet. She describes the outline of her young adult life: married to a Cambridge academic at the age of 22, three children by the age of 29, her decision to be sterilized after her third child, her struggle to write while raising young children. Rich then examines the many assumptions her younger self had accepted as inevitable: that her experience as a mother was simply “the human condition;” that motherhood and child care had always looked this way; that mothers acted on instinct alone; that the only person developing in the mother-child relationship was the child. Rich ends the chapter citing her hope and belief that culture will come to see female biology “as a resource, rather than a destiny.”

=== The Sacred Calling ===
Rich traces the shifting roles of women in the United States and England over the 19th century, and illustrates how women went from essential, widely-skilled, productive members of their homesteads in pre-industrial eras to isolated individuals whose role was limited to “the specialization of motherhood.” She describes how the growth of factories in the Industrial Revolution separated the home from the “man’s world” of wage-earning, ambition, and power, and created the ideal of the home as the “woman’s sphere” of refuge and retreat, a relatively recent concept in human history. “The home thus defined had never before existed. It was a creation of the Industrial Revolution, an ideal invested with the power of something God-given, and its power as an idea remains unexpunged today.” She identifies the repercussions of this shift for women and mothers: isolation, loneliness, powerlessness, and a narrow definition of a woman’s capacities.

===The Kingdom of the Fathers ===
In this chapter, Rich explores the roots, characteristics, and consequences of patriarchy, which she defines as “the power of the fathers.” She identifies the advent of private property and inherited wealth as key foundations of patriarchal order, and a tendency to think in “positive-negative polarities”—rational/irrational, powerful/powerless—as key characteristics. Power itself, Rich states, and power over others, “is a primal relationship under patriarchy,” most often exemplified through a man’s control over his wife and children. Monotheism, in which an all-powerful, usually male god, causes this patriarchal power structure to become “internalized as ‘conscience,’ ‘tradition,’ ‘the moral law within.” Rich discusses how women have mostly experienced power as a negative force. She identifies the renewed interest in matriarchal and pre-patriarchal cultures that characterized feminist and counter-culture movements of the 1960’s and 1970’s as efforts “to reintegrate what has been named the unconscious, the subjective, the emotional with the structural, the rational, the intellectual.”

Title: Embodied Movable Antennas

Abstract:
This paper introduces embodied movable antennas (MAs), a new MA architecture that rethinks the source of antenna mobility. Unlike conventional MAs that rely on dedicated antenna actuators, embodied MAs harness the mechanical degrees of freedom already present in physical agents to reconfigure antenna position and orientation. We distinguish two modes of embodied MAs: task-coupled and task-preserving. Focusing on the latter, we show how wireless channels can be reconfigured by exploiting task-equivalent host configurations without altering the prescribed physical task. Using a redundant robotic manipulator as a canonical realization, we characterize the intrinsically coupled antenna translation and orientation induced by task-preserving self-motion and derive an exact Fourier representation of the resulting multipath channel. Our analysis reveals that the wireless value of embodied mobility depends not merely on how far an antenna can move, but on which configurations remain feasible under the physical task and how their coupled motion interacts with polarization and multipath propagation. Building on this insight, we develop a cross-task antenna mounting design that enables wireless adaptation with a fixed physical installation. Numerical results demonstrate substantial communication gains through task-preserving motion. These findings establish mechanical redundancy as a new, quantifiable resource for wireless channel reconfiguration.

state.text: In 1992 I was an eager nineteen-year-old starting an apprenticeship as a furniture maker in Vermont, dreaming of one day opening my own workshop. Thirty years later I have that workshop, but the road there was not straight. My father, a carpenter who had taught me to hold a chisel, fell from a roof only six months into my training and broke his back. My mother had died years earlier, so I chose to leave the apprenticeship and look after him at home. Later I married and we had three daughters. Money was tight, so I took factory work and built small tables in the garage at night. It took me eleven more years to finish a part-time training course. My girls often asked why I was always in the garage, and there were nights I nearly quit. But I wanted them to see that a dream can wait without dying. Big goals, I learned, are reached one small cut at a time.
